technique_summary: Uses GPT-OSS-120B, an open-weight MoE LLM with about 12B active parameters per token, run on a single H100 80GB.
Wreath puzzles were deprioritized because simple beam search finds short solutions; the text does not detail what was submitted for them.
Focal loss with weight 1.0 is one component of the combined training loss.
LightGBM was tried and tuned but performed worse than XGBoost.
All experiments use 50 warm-up steps then linear decay to 10% of a 4e-6 peak learning rate.

technique_name: Species pseudo-classes from unique trait vectors
technique_summary: Training observations were grouped into 17,396 species classes by their unique trait values, following a public notebook, to enable classification heads.
Vision transformers underperformed convolutional encoders, which the author partly attributes to his own setup.

technique_name: Appending a metric-exploiting token string to predictions
technique_summary: A fixed suffix with repeated 'lucrarea' tokens, whose sentence-t5 embedding is close to the end-of-sequence token, was appended to predictions, pulling cosine similarity toward a high focal value and adding up to +0.05.
Selected the middle 10k/15k/20k outputs and resampled them with scipy.signal.resample rather than linear interpolation.
CatBoost is used as a base model in the ensemble.

technique_name: Parallel inference over scene subsets on two GPUs
technique_summary: The submission used Kaggle's T4 x2 environment and ran the pipeline in parallel on scene subsets split by dataset to fit more image pairs into the time limit.
High-entropy predictions were labelled 'Other'; the threshold was tuned on the public LB since no outliers were given. Authors report this raised public LB from 0.59 to 0.64.

technique_name: Solution described only in an external repository
technique_summary: The writeup contains no method description; it only points to an external code repository with an English/Japanese explanation of the solution, so no concrete technique can be extracted from this text.
CoT SFT used AdamW at 1e-4 learning rate with weight decay 0.01 and batch size 1024.
DINOv2 ViT-B and ViT-L backbones were used for image feature extraction.
Focal loss caused a noticeable score decrease compared with CE.
Cross-entropy with softmax was used since samples nearly always have a single label among 182 classes.
Supplemental external or simulated data did not work and was not used in the final solution.

technique_name: Manual injury adjustment of team ratings
technique_summary: For men only, player impact ratings were weighted by injury status (1.0/0.75/0.5) and subtracted from team net ratings.
Custom losses did not beat the standard binary focal loss, which the author found sufficient.
Xeno-Canto recordings (under 60 s) of extra Insecta/Amphibia species trained a dedicated model; extra target-species Xeno-Canto data usually hurt and was used by only one ensemble model.

technique_name: Blending position score and game outcome (WDL) as target
technique_summary: Stage 2 targets mixed a position score derived from lc0 Q values with the game result (WDL); stage 1 used only scores from a 5k-node search.
Random subsets were augmented with spelling correction, character edits, synonym replacement, obfuscations, back translation, random capitalization and sentence swaps.

technique_name: Patch cap per slide with Ray parallel processing
technique_summary: WSIs were capped at 200 patches and Ray processed two images at once on one P100 (detection, tiling, feature extraction), bringing runtime under 7 hours; RAM was the limit.
A GNN classifier built a KNN graph (25 nearest neighbours, Euclidean distance) over samples and used GraphSAGE to fit the target.
Used injury reports, manually entered player ratings and AP poll data in addition to competition data.

technique_name: Place cameras on a circle around transparent objects
technique_summary: For transparent scenes, ordered images are assigned evenly spaced camera poses on a circle facing the object instead of running SfM.
A dense autoencoder with a 4-node hidden layer trained with MSE denoises the dip spectrum; per-planet normalization and moving-median smoothing of the input were important.

technique_name: Pure chain-of-thought model with majority voting
technique_summary: Stage-1-only CoT models with maj@32 were limited (best 8/50 public) and discarded in favor of the TIR recipe.
Considered LEB128 variable-length encoding because most 16-bit weights fit in 8 bits, but the author found its compression insufficient.
Four lightly tuned XGBoost models (two target transforms by production/consumption) sharing the same 600 features formed the tree part of the solution.
Automated hyperparameter tuning with Optuna is noted as a missed opportunity.
A post-processing attempt to repair I-URL_PERSONAL predictions did not work.

technique_name: Target differenced and normalized by installed capacity
technique_summary: Models were trained on two target transforms: the 2-day difference divided by installed capacity, and target divided by installed capacity.
7-fold cross-validation split by experiment (tomogram); mean F4 over folds correlated well with the leaderboard.
An extra head predicts each target's loss (trained with MAE); a model with it reached 0.79159/0.78869 versus 0.78945/0.78631 without.
Model weight files were read before initialization so they sit in the Linux page cache, reducing disk access and startup latency.
TF-IDF and LSA text features did not work well.
A custom 3D MixUp implementation allowed longer training while preventing overfitting.
Features from raddar's notebook: provided data, seeds and seed difference, season-average box-score statistics for team and opponents, Elo ratings and a team-quality estimate.
Main loss predicts mean and variance (variance via softplus plus 1e-3), automatically downweighting high-variance samples; the author's ablation credits it with improving accuracy.
Unigram and trigram language models trained on the NLTK Brown corpus with the Llama tokenizer supply additional token probabilities.
Kept only three features for men and four for women, reporting their correlations with the outcome.
Submitted model used SmoothL1 for regression plus cross-entropy for interval classification (classification weight 0.3).
Used Leela Chess Zero training-run data (best from smaller T77/T79 networks) plus Stockfish-generated data previously prepared in binpack format by the author.
Augmenting the data with rare or multinational names did not work.

A seed-and-expand clustering using farthest point sampling and iterative MASt3R matching was built, but it gave no clear benefit over COLMAP multiple reconstructions and scored lower on public/private, so it was dropped.
Selected OOFs were combined with a Ridge meta-model, chosen for stability with correlated predictions and lower overfitting.
Gradient clipping threshold raised to 64.0 for both models, following earlier LMSYS solutions.
Scalar (non-level) features use simple mean/std standardization.
TabM is one of the strongest single models and was heavily hyperparameter-tuned.
RegNetY-008 and RegNetY-016 backbones were used; the final ensemble has two RegNetY-016 models from iteration 4 and one supervised RegNetY-008.
Llama 7B and TinyLlama 1.1B replaced OpenAI models for Ghostbuster token probabilities; fine-tuning TinyLlama on PERSUADE gave a small boost.
Transformer models such as DeBERTa-v3 were tried for external score prediction but never beat TF-IDF + LightGBM.
Models trained on different datasets served as teachers for a student on other data with the same folds, using weighted CE plus temperature-scaled KL loss; reported +0.005-0.01 CV/LB.
Simulated annealing selects a set of candidate subqueries joined by OR; moves add or remove one subquery with equal probability and the score is the number of target patents retrieved.
Stage 2 data was synthesized by prompting GPT-4 for ToRA-style solutions with code execution feedback, approximating the DeepSeekMath Instruct/RL data.
Tversky and Dice losses were listed under what did not work; weighted cross-entropy was kept.

technique_name: Time and frequency masking on spectrograms
technique_summary: XY (time/frequency) masking augmentation was applied to spectrograms.
Plain log(x) normalization did not work, distinct from the log-style representation that was used.
Tournaments are simulated 5000 times to produce the portfolio of brackets required by the 2024 format, approximating the rating-implied probabilities.
Added Moire patterns, flares and overlaid non-rectified images to harden training and improve robustness.
Trained with SmoothL1 loss and AdamW (lr 1e-4) at batch size 1.
Enabled DeepCache (cache_interval=2, cache_branch_id=0) to accelerate diffusion sampling.
Feeding multiple days instead of a single day to the GRU did not work.
CatBoost on the base+bin+digit+categorical feature set was among the frequently selected models.
DeBERTa-v3 large (occasionally base) regression models with 1024 context are the backbone; final ensembles were mostly DeBERTa large.
CoT SFT used 10% linear warmup then decay to 1e-7; TIR fine-tuning used a constant 1e-5 learning rate for 400 steps.
The neural model was LightAutoML's DenseLight dense network (with some library bugs fixed by the author); no larger model beat it.
The segmentation architecture is a U-Net from segmentation_models_pytorch with a ConvNeXt-Tiny encoder.

technique_name: Filter samples by annotator vote count
technique_summary: The shared validation strategy lists a vote count of at least 10 as a criterion; the text does not detail it further.
Added three visible characters in the top-left corner; a search over three-letter combinations selected the string with the best average aesthetic score without hurting VQA.
Gemini-generated prompts and community reasoning templates were evaluated but the original notebook prompt was used instead.
Dice loss with weight 1.0 is part of the combined loss.
Training combined the BELKA train set with an external DEL dataset from a published paper, preprocessed by another participant.
Instead of image retrieval, image pairs are kept when they have at least 30 matches for a single detector and 100 across the detector ensemble, filtering pairs gradually.
Soft and hard pseudo-labeling did not improve CV.
The regression target was efs_time ranked and normalized separately within the efs groups.
Weighted cross-entropy over 7 classes with positive particle pixels weighted 256 versus 1 for background to handle the very small number of positive pixels.
Six early-round men's games where the model was not confident in the higher seed were manually pushed toward ~0.95-0.98, citing expert opinion.
A diverse set of template-based and template-free models was combined; authors believe diversity helped on harder private targets without close templates.
Each tomogram was resized to a fixed (128, 704, 704) volume with scipy.ndimage.zoom.
Used 1000+ per-tile features on the 24x24 map; features were encoded both as normalized continuous values and as binned one-hot vectors.
Extracted integer digit positions and leading decimal digits from numeric variables as extra features (BIN+DIGIT sets appear in top single models).
LightGBM with DART boosting is a base model; DART improved LightGBM by about 0.004 CV and 0.003 LB at a 5-10x training-time cost.
Besides balanced sampling, class weights were applied in the cross-entropy loss to handle subtype imbalance.
A genetic algorithm over islands arranged on a ring, with mechanisms that exchange genetic material while preventing any single solution from dominating the population.
Few-shot prompted Llama 3.1 70B and Qwen 2.5 32B generated additional rulesets; most failed to compile or were low quality, leaving 93 in the extra data.
Blended long lead II into lead II and, when relations nearly hold, softly enforced II = I + III and aVR + aVL + aVF = 0; authors report this added about 0.06.
Protenix provides one prediction for short sequences and two for sequences of 1000 nt or more.
Final solution ensembles 3D segmentation U-Nets with MONAI object detection models (SegResNet and DynUnet backbones) from the teammate's detection pipeline.
7B models were fast but scored lower on CV and LB; 32B CoT models fit but scored close to 14B, so 14B was kept.

technique_name: Weighted voting ensemble of token classifiers
technique_summary: Final predictions came from weighted voting over 7 model groups (10 models), mixing fold and full-fit models for diversity.
MAE loss outperformed MSE despite the R-squared metric, converging faster and more stably; the author calls it the main non-leak secret.
Oversampling hard negatives by OOF log-loss difficulty was listed as not working.
Genetic diversity is the minimal per-tree transformation between solutions (modulo mirror/90-degree rotation), computed with the Hungarian algorithm or a faster approximation in CUDA.
Team strength came from Nate Silver's external power ratings for men's and women's teams rather than a trained model.
Feature set 1 (best for neural nets) includes cyclical features taken from public notebooks by another competitor.

technique_name: Extra detector keypoints matched with MASt3R
technique_summary: Inspired by MP-SfM, ALIKED (1280px, 4096 kpts) and SuperPoint (1600px, 4096 kpts) keypoints are additionally matched using MASt3R features alongside the semi-dense matches, which improved the score.
The inference pipeline hit GPU memory and disk limits even with two models; a ChatGPT-assisted redesign made a 4-model ensemble feasible.
Using betting or prediction-market odds was identified as sensible but not done.
Tried many shaped rewards (relic points, damage, deaths, sensor range, exploration, etc.) before moving to a sparse match-result scheme.
Unlabeled soundscapes were pseudo-labeled by the best previous ensemble and used in Noisy Student-style self-training for 4 iterations with progressively larger backbones, each boosting public LB.
Because of high seed variance on ~4.5k fine-tuning samples, every model was averaged over 3 seeds at train and inference; only the fine-tuning stage was re-run per seed to save compute.
A 4-layer GRU modeled each stock's 55 time steps within a day, predicting all steps at once from the shared 300 features.
Each final ensemble uses its own probability threshold (0.20 for Set 1, 0.26 for Set 2).
Transformer variants, including one from a prior winning solution, were tried without success.
More TMA patches via 30-80% overlapping sliding windows greatly increased runtime (many notebook timeouts) and did not improve performance.
Open-source LLMs were fine-tuned on PERSUADE via metadata instruction tuning, held-out-prompt generation and span-wise generation to produce new writing styles.
TF-IDF features were reduced to 64 dimensions with truncated SVD.

technique_name: Judge-specific score splitting via prompt injection
technique_summary: Built three families of essays, each designed so one judge model gives 0 while the other two give 9, maximizing disagreement among judges.
Hyperparameter tuning of the best models (RealMLP, TabM, GBDTs) while saving OOF predictions from every trial and adding them to the ensemble improved LB from about 8.5335 to 8.5309.
Models are optimized with AdamW.
Training uses the RAdam optimizer for 210 epochs, evaluated every 6 epochs.
Pseudo labels were listed among approaches that did not work.
Out-of-fold image model predictions became features for the GBDT models; at test time predictions from same-type models were averaged.
ResNet34 is one of the two encoder backbones used in the 3D U-Net segmentation models.
Quantized the model (FP8 in the final pipeline per the TL;DR) for faster inference than BF16 and more KV-cache memory; INT4 was measured with notably lower accuracy.
RNN architectures were tried without success.
Several model variants were trained, and heads from different models were combined with manually chosen weights in a mixture-of-experts style.

technique_name: Surface fitting to remove grid-point outliers
technique_summary: Improved the rectification step with sub-pixel grid point estimates via weighted averaging and surface fitting to drop outlier grid points and fill gaps.
Using top CatBoost-importance features, a Local Outlier Factor score per lesion within each patient captured how atypical a lesion is for that patient; improved CV and LB.

technique_name: Averaging overlapping framewise predictions across chunks
technique_summary: Instead of taking only the central 5 s, framewise SED outputs from overlapping 20 s chunks were averaged (like sliding-window segmentation/TTA), with edge padding removed afterwards.
Used a modified fishtest dev server running SPRT tests to measure Elo changes, plus quick local fixed-node checks with fastchess, as the main way to quantify engine progress.

technique_name: Unsplit agent strings as categorical features
technique_summary: Using whole agent strings as categorical features did not work well.
Back-translation augmentation did not work.
CatBoost parameters were tuned with Optuna on tabular-only features and not retuned after adding image-model features; other models were not tuned.
An auxiliary deep-supervision head on the second-to-last feature map contributed to the loss.
Added a pool of older frozen agents as opponents once pure self-play plateaued, to improve robustness and avoid overfitting to one self-play style.
Held out the first ten training IDs, using three image types each (30 images) for validation.
CatBoost trained up to 1000 iterations with early stopping (od_wait 100), with parameters chosen by Optuna on tabular data.
A simple 2.5D model was tried for severity but MIL performed better in the end.
Mixed precision on the T4x2 hardware significantly reduced image matching time.
Because Chowder is sensitive to initialization, each fold trained 50 Chowder models differing only by init, which was more stable than a single model.
Separate bird-call detection models performed close to random/constant prediction.
Implemented mixing behavior-cloning batches from replays of a strong team into RL batches, but did not use it because RL alone was already improving strongly.
A logistic regression on ImageNet ResNet18 thumbnail features classified test images as TMA vs WSI to choose the tiling setup.

technique_name: Hash size tuning under RAM limit
technique_summary: Measured error-loss rates versus hash size near the 5mb RAM limit and chose an 896kb hash for the final submissions, accepting a 3-4% error-loss rate.
Computed possessions, pace and offensive/defensive/net efficiency per game from box scores as inputs to a custom team rating.

technique_name: Periodic online retraining during test period
technique_summary: Models were retrained on newly revealed data every 12 days; the best submission hit the time limit, so only 4 updates ran, and online learning improved test scores in the reported table.
Half-cosine learning-rate decay schedule from a 1e-3 peak.
Predictions were centered by subtracting the stock-weight-weighted mean rather than the plain mean, consistent with the target definition.
Adding external data did not work.

technique_name: MLM pretraining from scratch with small vocabulary
technique_summary: Training DeBERTa-v3-xsmall from scratch as an MLM with a 55-token custom vocabulary on q-masked text failed to get below 0.63.
Regressor training weighted efs==1 and efs==0 samples 0.6:0.4.
BCE and focal losses gave similar results when tuned but were slightly worse than CE, so they were not used.

technique_name: Local LLM judge proxies for validation
technique_summary: Candidate essays/attacks were validated locally against three judge LLMs (Gemma, Qwen, Phi) assumed to mirror the hidden judges.

technique_name: Noise injection for selected race groups
technique_summary: Adding noise for some race groups improved CV considerably but did not help on public or private LB.
Plain averaging of all OOF predictions hurt performance compared with selected subsets.
Final inference matched patch height/width to the volume and slid only along depth with 0.875 overlap, about 4x faster than the original pipeline at similar score.
Images were only scaled by dividing by 65535 (16-bit range) with no other normalization.
Each model's outputs were calibrated with a logistic regression fit on its internal validation split, which slightly improved public LB.

technique_name: Predict traits via species classification lookup
technique_summary: A classification head predicts the species and outputs that species' trait values.
Training used the first 500 days with the remaining days as a holdout, which tracked the leaderboard well; only the overall ensemble score was monitored.
The main trick: a short Ludii MCTS search (UCB1Tuned, random playouts, ~15 s) on each game's starting position yields game-balance features, improving ~0.045 CV and ~0.012 LB.
LLMs were loaded as AutoModelForSequenceClassification with max length 1024, 2 epochs and global batch size 64.

technique_name: Monthly retraining on newly revealed data
technique_summary: Expecting 8 more months of data in the private period, the author traded a larger ensemble for fewer models retrained monthly; updates improved test scores in the reported table.
Mixup was applied to every training sample.
During inference, generated code blocks were executed in a sandbox and the output or error trace appended before generation continued.
Changed quantization constants from the defaults (QA=255, QB=64) to QA=101, QB=160, trading weight precision against the size limit.
A physically motivated wind magnitude from u and v components was added; it neither helped nor hurt.
Nonlinear stacking meta-models overfit and did not improve CV.
Applied the community ptend trick for a range of moisture tendency targets (ptend_q0002_2 to 26).

technique_name: Transposing weight layout to improve compression
technique_summary: Observed that storing correlated weights sequentially compresses better, so transposing the feature-transformer weight matrix reduces binary size; whether it was in the final build is not explicitly stated.
tf_efficientnet B0/B3/B4 (Noisy Student weights) backbones were used across stages; the final ensemble included B4, B3 and a B0 Amphibia/Insecta model.
Mel spectrograms (224 mel bins, large hop size for speed with long chunks, 0-1 normalized) repeated to 3 channels formed the input; more mel bins helped distinguish narrow-band species.
Label-dependent epsilon-insensitive L1 loss gave their best single model on private LB but was not in the submitted model.
Each full 630x630x184 tomogram is standardized by its mean and standard deviation before patch extraction.
Models were exported via JIT or TensorRT for inference, reported as a 200% speedup that allowed a slightly larger ensemble within the time limit.
The final NuminaMath-7B-TIR model was fine-tuned from DeepSeekMath-Base 7B, which the team found hard to beat because of its math-focused continued pretraining.
Inputs were generated two ways: homography to 3200x2400 then grid remapping, or remapping directly on the rotated image; a one-image local test favored high-resolution remapping over low-resolution.
A DINOv2 ViT pretrained on PlantCLEF 2024 southwestern European flora (Pl@ntNet images) gave a significant boost.
TRL SFTTrainer packing concatenated samples into 2048-token chunks to speed up training.
Repeated (3x) stratified 5-fold CV with an inner 75/25 train/validation split; folds were designed so test folds held at least 60% of TMAs, keeping most TMAs for evaluation.
Tuned engine parameters with SPSA for sudden-death time controls, using 20s instead of 10s to account for delay and pondering.
Applied stochastic dropout for regularization of the encoder.
Newline and double-space tokens were added to the tokenizer, following a tip shared by another participant.
No effective method for separating touching sheets was found; the team relied on nnU-Net itself to limit them.

technique_name: Different opening verb per model for diversity
technique_summary: Each model was prompted with a different opening verb to diversify the concatenated predictions, raising the score from 0.70 to 0.71.
GBDT was weak alone and as a second stage added nothing over the ensemble plus thresholding, though limited time was spent on it.
A multi-sample dropout DeBERTa variant gave smoother training curves with fewer spikes; listed among variations tried for the ensemble without explicit confirmation of final use.
Model was a U-Net-like 3D network with a single deconvolution block in the decoder before the segmentation head.
Listed as an idea the author did not get around to trying.
TabM tabular neural network was one of the classifiers, also in a rank-loss variant, used in the classifier-regressor combinations.
TabNet (CV 0.609) was included among the NN base models.
An external English Word Frequency dataset supplied one of the signals for keyword priors.
Each model block averages the 20 models from 10-fold CV repeated for 2 seeds, instead of a full-data refit.
Stage-two pre-training predicted 2048-bit chiral ECFP fingerprints from SMILES with frozen embeddings; though MAP was only ~0.4, the author credits it for learning useful representations.
A play-level model with a 3-layer Transformer encoder over up to 22 players models inter-player interactions, using player masks for variable counts and SwiGLU FFNs.
Rebound and free-throw rate (and most other tried features) made the model worse and were dropped.
The winning submission averaged predictions of 65 Chowder models from selected CV repetitions/folds rather than all 750 trained models.
Tomograms were ranked by max predicted value and the lowest quantile predicted as no motor; the quantile was tuned on public LB (0.565 public optimum, 0.560 private).
A boundary loss (arXiv 1812.07032) with small weight 0.01 is added to the combined loss.
SIFT, GIMSuperPoint and DaD were tried as additional keypoint detectors but not adopted because ALIKED+SuperPoint gave the best LB score.
XGBoost was tried but did not work well.
Reimplemented the metric's image processing pipeline more efficiently so candidate SVGs could be scored locally.
Final essays are reconstructed from the keystroke logs using public essay-constructor notebooks and used for text features and NLP models.
Delta-shift TTA, borrowed from the 2nd place BirdCLEF 2023 solution, was applied at inference.
Larger dimensions (64), smaller (16), and models deeper than 6 layers did not perform as well as the small 32-dim, 4-layer encoder.

technique_name: Template-based structure modeling via sequence alignment
technique_summary: Global pairwise alignment against train+validation structures, keeping length-compatible top-30 templates; TBM is the primary predictor for sequences of 250 nt or more.
Initial approach used 3D Gaussian balls as segmentation targets; it was replaced by single-pixel targets after analysis of the detection model.
Because disk loading was slow, all augmentations except rescaling ran on the GPU; rescaling used fast order-0 zoom.
1D-CNN models were tried but did not work.
Three-fold CV with folds grouped jointly by state and sampling date; single-fold models were trained.
InceptionNeXt small/base backbones were in the ensemble alongside HGNetV2-B6, MambaOut-base and CAFormer-M36.
A final binary_fill_holes pass on the whole mask fills cavities of arbitrary size.
Three KNN-regressor prediction features based on word-length statistics, text_change statistics and punctuation-only TF-IDF.

technique_name: Covert leaderboard testing of stronger model
technique_summary: To test on the leaderboard while hiding strength from imitation learners, a submission played a proven model 85% of the time and a new model 15%, logging which played; later, logits noise weakened submissions.
GBDT training kept the public notebook's undersampling of the majority (benign) class.
Men's and women's tournaments were modeled separately with their own features, hyperparameters and calibrators.

technique_name: Capacity x solar radiation / temperature interaction feature
technique_summary: A feature from a public discussion combining installed capacity, forecast solar radiation and temperature helped by about 0.1-0.2.

Because the new essays seemed scored with different criteria, models were pre-trained on old Persuade data and fine-tuned on the new data, giving at least +0.015 public LB and better CV-LB correlation.
An SVM classifier on the Ghostbuster features, ensembled with a random forest, replaced logistic regression.
Optical-flow magnitude (std better than mean) was an earlier ordering weight in the timeline, superseded by the SSIM + matching ensemble.

technique_name: Classifier and regressor combined by a parametric merge function
technique_summary: Survival scoring was decomposed into a classifier for P(efs=0) and a regressor ranking efs_time among efs=1 patients; a parametric merge function (params a, b, c) combines them, followed by a rank transform.

technique_name: Multiview 2.5D slicing along x, y, z
technique_summary: Training slices are taken from all three axes of the 3D volume and fed as 3-slice 2.5D inputs.
A patch is discarded if it increases the number of holes, which can happen on strongly curved sheets.
Cosine annealing with warm restarts every 5 epochs allowed longer training than a single cycle.

To blend segmentation and detection feature maps with different distributions, per-class rank-based value replacement matches B's distribution to A's before blending and running detection post-processing.
Kept the best model so far as a frozen teacher and added a KL loss between student and teacher policies plus a teacher value-baseline loss to prevent forgetting.

technique_name: Use only the AIRS-CH0 instrument channel
technique_summary: Only AIRS-CH0 data was used, since the method relies on adjacent-wavelength correlation and the FGS1 channel's distorted PSF made it hard to use.
Shift-scale-rotate augmentation (shift 0.1, scale +-0.1, rotate 20 degrees, p=0.5) after cropping.
Pruning layers of larger models based on activation similarity did not beat simply using gemma-2-9b.
Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct answered general questions about the keyword in the Answerer role.
Prompt refinement was reported as more impactful than several complex optimizations; the original public-notebook prompt was kept in the end.
Final model is a linear weight merge of a student trained on all data and one trained without the last two (nbroad and synthetic) datasets.
The IMC23 winners' DFSFM refinement was tested but timed out in submission even with parallelism and gave only small validation gains, so it was not used.
When an island's overlap falls below a threshold its square boundary is shrunk, so islands can work at different square sizes.
TBM outputs are corrected for bond lengths, angles, Laplacian smoothing and steric clashes, with strength inversely scaled by template similarity.

technique_name: Custom C tiler using libpng row reads
technique_summary: Custom C code built on libpng (png_read_row) tiled huge PNGs while limiting RAM use, compiled inside the Kaggle notebook.
Fixed 5-fold stratified splits shared across all base models and the ensemble to avoid stacking leakage; scored by overall OOF AUC.
Selected one pure-model submission with best CV and one with the metric hack applied, hedging against the hack not working.
In-line approximations (convex-breakdown separation distance, overlapping area) were tried instead of the lookup table and did not work as well.
Plain MLPs were listed among things that did not work well and were beaten by TabM.
A text CNN reached about 0.63 CV and did not improve the ensemble.
CatBoost and TabM depend on early stopping, which is why fold models are ensembled rather than trained on all data.
The 5 fold LoRA adapters were merged by directly averaging their weights into one model.
Linear interpolation gave lower SNR than Fourier resampling in a single-image local comparison, so it was not used.
For cube clusters (reduced by symmetry to a few small-cube cases), bidirectional search enumerated all shortest 3-rots; the longest needed 14 moves.
Coordinate models were first pretrained on a community coordinate dataset, which was slightly better than ImageNet-only pretraining.
ImageNet-pretrained RegNetY-008 was the second backbone, used in one of the two final ensembles.
Using the PLR (periodic-linear-ReLU) continuous embedder in DenseLight improved CV by 0.01 and public LB by 0.004.
To limit overfitting with 27 combinations, Optuna weight search was bounded to [0.1, 1], which the author views as regularization.
Pseudo-labelling the test data did not work.
LoRA/DoRA were deliberately not used; the team did full fine-tuning because they doubted PEFT would match it without much experimentation.
Equal blending weights were used to limit overfitting to the public LB.

technique_name: Split long audio into fixed segments treated as separate files
technique_summary: Audio was split into X-second segments (20/30/60 tried, 60 in the step table) treated as separate files, balancing many short train files against few long soundscapes.
First TBM prediction uses the best template; extra TBM slots sample from the top-12 with exponential weights and a 0.1x penalty on reused templates.
Among mergekit methods, a linear merge (0.3 CoT + 0.7 TIR) worked best, improving maj@16 accuracy while shortening outputs and reducing code executions versus pure TIR.
Climate and soil metadata were processed by a structured self-attention module to model correlations among metadata and with traits, important for traits like nitrogen content and seed dry mass.
Unaligned residues are filled by linear interpolation of C1' coordinates, terminal gaps extrapolated at 5.95 A steps, with a linear fallback if no template exists.
50k synthetic pairs from lmsys-chat-1m prompts filtered to complexity >=3 with matched language and domain mix; responses sampled via vLLM from large open models and soft-labeled by teachers.
For even tree counts only half the trees are free and the other half are their 180-degree rotations, enforced through a genotype/phenotype split; this halves degrees of freedom.

technique_name: Custom tokenizer from train and test essays
technique_summary: A tokenizer fit on train and test essays was used for a DeBERTa-v3-small model to specialize on the hidden test set.
On top of a public notebook's features, total lesion area per patient and per patient plus anatomical site was added.

Isotonic regression was applied to OOFs before and after Ridge and was in the submitted ensemble; afterwards the author found that without it the ensemble was slightly worse on public LB but better on private LB.
Horizontal (time-axis) CutMix was used and gave a notable gain in the step table.
Auxiliary spacetime targets (lat/lon, day/year cycle sin/cos) were predicted with MAE; host-confirmed as legitimate, but a no-auxiliary ensemble scored similarly.
SWA gave a negligible change in score.
Added rank and mean-ratio features computed across stocks within the same seconds_in_bucket time step.
DeBERTa token classifiers with 13 labels, max length 1600-2048, 3-4 epochs, LR 1e-5, formed the ensemble; DeBERTa was chosen for fast inference and good CV/LB.
Coarse dropout (cutout-style masking) was applied with 50% probability.
One image of each pair is rotated by 0/90/180/270 degrees and the rotation yielding the most matches is kept, handling images not in natural orientation.
Used bfloat16 reduced-precision training as a performance booster for training at a scale of about 1.5B environment steps for the final model.
With probability 0.2, the image is shrunk by a factor of 0.85-1.0 and placed at a random position on a black canvas to mimic camera focal-length/view differences.

technique_name: Synthetic long-reasoning solution generation with teacher LLMs
technique_summary: Generated 3.2M chain-of-thought solutions (temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95) with DeepSeek-R1 and QwQ-32B; the submission used the 2.2M DeepSeek-R1 subset.
Difference features between individual income, expenses and taxes did not help.
Attention in the MASt3R/DUSt3R/CroCo code was replaced with torch scaled_dot_product_attention to enable flash attention and speed up the pipeline.
A default ForSequenceClassification head with two output classes predicts which response wins.

technique_name: Inserting 3-rots at the best position in the sequence
technique_summary: Instead of appending 3-rots, an equivalent 3-rot is inserted at every possible time step and the position giving the shortest sequence or most cancellations is chosen.
With poor CV/LB correlation, ideas were judged on public LB using 2-5 fold-model ensembles to reduce seed noise; public scores correlated well with private.
The LightGBM model used a smaller feature set, dropping mainly categorical items that degraded performance or caused overfitting.
CatBoost was used as classifier and regressor, with an optimal depth of 6; it had the highest classifier AUC in the reported table.
Pseudo-labeled Feedback Prize 2/3 essays added to DeBERTa training did not help.
Three TTA variants using gamma changes plus crop/resize of the Stage 1 inputs; reported gain of 0.07.
An EfficientNetV2-M backbone was one of the ensembled models (5056x1280 input, strategy 2).
Extra Persuade and Ellipse essays were judged neutral or unsure, making little difference.
NN, TabNet/TabM and GNN classifiers were also trained with a pairwise rank loss and these rank models were part of the 9 classifiers.
VGGT's tracking head on pre-extracted keypoints looked good locally (best on the stairs scene) but caused a TimeoutError in submission, so it could not be used.
Listed under what didn't work: MLM pretraining.

technique_name: Image-retrieval pair shortlist (union of multiple global features)
technique_summary: Candidate image pairs come from the union of retrieval neighbors using MASt3R-ASMK, MASt3R-SPoC, DINOv2 and ISC global features (top-10 each); more pairs raised the score, and this mix was faster than heavier ASMK-only settings.
Within-cluster Z-scores of moles slightly improved CV and public LB but not private LB; listed under what didn't work.
An attention pooling head did not work.
Gemma-7b-1.1-it was also part of the model mix; no single model exceeded 0.65 on its own.
Models were quantized to 8-bit with AutoGPTQ using training data for calibration, halving upload time and fitting 2xT4; the small accuracy drop was offset by sampling many candidates.
Larger models did not beat DeepSeek 7B and had slow inference with unexplained timeouts.
Gemma2-9B, a student fine-tuned with LoRA and distillation from the 70B teachers, was the submitted model.
A single time-based holdout: first 400 days for training, last 81 days for validation; CV aligned well with the leaderboard.
The merged model was quantized to 8-bit with GPTQ for submission.
Lagged key up/down time features from the keystroke log.
Replaced hand-crafted evaluation with a tiny NNUE: 768 piece-square inputs, dual perspective, a single hidden layer; the author reports a simple network with good data beating HCE by about 100 Elo.

technique_name: Gradient checkpointing with DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 sharding
technique_summary: Gradient checkpointing and ZeRO-3 sharding let weights, gradients and optimizer states fit in VRAM; training took 10 hours on 8 H100s.
CPU inference was sped up with OpenVINO compilation, parallel mel computation with joblib and caching spectrograms in RAM, allowing a 6-model ensemble in about 2 hours.
Transformer models were listed under what did not work.
CutMix augmentation was tried to improve generalization but gave unsatisfactory results.
Feature set 1 target-encodes selected feature combinations with mean, std and skew statistics.

technique_name: Repeat reconstruction with relaxed match threshold
technique_summary: For scenes with few registered images, reconstruction is repeated with a relaxed match threshold and the reconstruction with more registered images is kept.
Particle centers are encoded as single-pixel targets instead of Gaussian heatmaps, made workable by down-weighting the background class.

technique_name: Other MIL models (DeepMIL, DSMIL, TransMIL, MeanPool)
technique_summary: DeepMIL, DSMIL, TransMIL and MeanPool were considered but Chowder outperformed them; the winning submission used only Chowder.
Two-view geometry is estimated with RANSAC outside COLMAP rather than with COLMAP's internal implementation.
Inference packs sequences without padding, adapted from a previous LMSYS 2nd-place solution for Qwen2.5.
Xeno-canto additional data, even filtered by Google classifier/BirdNet or statistics, reduced the score; final submissions used only 2024 data.

technique_name: Self-play win-rate evaluation against older versions
technique_summary: Compared agents via thousands of matches and real-time win rates against older versions and the teacher model.
Ridge on word-level TF-IDF n-grams of reconstructed essays had weak CV (~0.628) but significantly improved the ensemble.
Enforcing 90-degree symmetry produced good but never optimal solutions, so it was not used.

For large N, initial solutions place inner trees on a predetermined two-tree crystal (the 'Perfect dimer' was hardest to beat) and GA moves touch only edge trees; relaxation still moves all trees. Enables going up to N=200.
Pseudo-labeled test essays were added to training, followed by one epoch of training and inference on the test set.
Ghostbuster-style features: token probabilities from two LLMs and unigram/trigram models, combined via ratios and 10 summary operations into 100 features.
Cube and globe puzzles are solved with move sequences that cycle exactly three pieces (3-rot), which exist for almost every cluster of interchangeable pieces.

technique_name: Intersecting posting sets in ascending size order
technique_summary: Words are added smallest posting set first since intersection cost is bounded by the smaller set.
Listed under what didn't work: freezing layers.
Built a training problem set of 540K unique math problems extracted and refined from AoPS forum posts with an LLM-based pipeline.
A probability threshold of 0.4 was used, chosen from a CV/LB optimum of roughly 0.4 to 0.5.
Feature engineering was plain aggregation per item: max, min, mean, variance, first, last and max-min range.

technique_name: Per-image DBSCAN crop of matched regions
technique_summary: Frequently matched keypoints are clustered with DBSCAN to crop one representative region per image (instead of per-pair IMC2022 crops); it consistently improved local results.
Non-transparent scenes are reconstructed by an SfM module built on COLMAP; transparent scenes use a separate direct pose module.
Slices are upscaled at inference: a dynamic scale factor targeting about 3200x3200 area for the selected submission, and a fixed 3072x3072 resize for the best-scoring one.
Each image prediction divided by the patient's mean prediction (with the same noise) was added and consistently improved CV and LB.
Treating scoring as classification with DeBERTa did not work; regression was used instead.
Image augmentations were reused from a previous SIIM-ISIC melanoma competition solution.
Two-phase training: large CoT SFT first, then a short 400-step TIR fine-tune on 15K samples starting from the CoT model.
Segmentation part uses MONAI FlexibleUnet (3D U-Net) trained from scratch with ResNet34 and EfficientNet-B3 encoders; relatively small models worked well.
After the GA stops, a relaxation variant adapted to reach a true zero-overlap solution removes the remaining small overlaps.
XGBoost hyperparameters (eta 0.0093, subsample 0.6, max_depth 4, num_parallel_tree 2, max_bin 38, etc.) were tuned further, lowering the Brier score.
All features are matchup differentials, including seed difference, custom rating difference and quality-wins difference (plus blocks for women).

technique_name: Coarse solve with short sequences before 3-rot
technique_summary: Because each 3-rot costs at least 8 moves, the puzzle is first brought near-solved with elementary moves and short sequences, using 3-rots only for final touches.
The Transformer output was centered by subtracting its mean across stocks, which the author found helpful.
Extra rows get lower sample weights tuned per model on CV (CatBoost 0.25, LightGBM 1.0, TabM 0.5) to offset label noise.
BCE, including with positive weights, gave noticeably worse scores than CE.
Using an STFT spectrogram instead of mel noticeably decreased the score.
Separate isotonic calibrators fit on OOF predictions for men and women, clipped to 0.001-0.999; improved CV Brier for both.
Prompt and both responses are concatenated, and each part is proportionally truncated from the middle when the sample exceeds the maximum length.
Sampled actions stochastically during training but chose the most probable action in Kaggle inference.
Adding random noise to features as augmentation did not work well.
Transformer-style tabular models (TabNet, TabTransformer, FT-Transformer) were listed as not working.

technique_name: Unsupervised similarity-based scoring with weak labels
technique_summary: Variant of a public unsupervised approach: confident Mistral predictions provide weak labels, neighbors chosen by dynamic threshold, and similarity scores mean-aggregated.
LightGBM served as classifier and regressor; the author found max depth 2 optimal for LightGBM and XGBoost, suggesting little useful feature interaction.
Multistage schemes (train_audio then soundscapes or vice versa, full-data then finetune) decreased the score; pretraining on previous years gave negligible change.

technique_name: Uncertainty as weighted mix of constant, spread and GP std
technique_summary: Predicted sigma is a weighted average of a constant, the per-planet std of the smoothed predicted spectrum, and the GP's predicted uncertainty.
Other drafting approaches were tried but did not work as well as ReDrafter; the authors note LLM drafting might still be better.

technique_name: Multiple random hold-out sets plus public LB
technique_summary: Four 100K-sample validation sets were used; at full data scale local validation decorrelated from LB, so final models and ensembling were judged on public LB.
DeBERTa-v3-base regression on reconstructed essays (best CV 0.61083); final version trained 8 models for 10 epochs on all essays.
Shallow XGBRegressor (depth 2, lr 0.003, up to 4000 trees with early stopping) regressing the win indicator, with gender-specific hyperparameters.
Model outputs were combined with min() rather than mean to suppress noisy sigmoid predictions; a min ensemble of 6 EfficientNet-B0 was a selected final submission.
Two final strategies were run in parallel; the ensemble tuned purely on CV beat the LB-tuned one on both public and private leaderboards.
Dynamic feature encoder of seven unpadded depthwise Conv1d layers reduces 20 frames to a single final-frame embedding of 640 dims per player; the decoder also uses Conv1d layers to output 48 frames.
Linear regression (CV 0.572) and logistic classifier stacking were reported as ensemble options; which one formed the winning submission is not stated explicitly.
The solution builds on prior public work (credited to Parthenos) and empirical benchmarking of public notebooks.
For each classifier-regressor pair (27 combinations), the merge-function parameters a, b, c were tuned with 5-fold CV to produce merged predictions.

technique_name: Fitting known-gas absorption spectra with TauREx3
technique_summary: Fitting dip spectra with TauREx3 known-gas absorption worked on train but scored horribly on LB, presumably due to atmospheric composition shift.
Star, tree and hypercube island connectivity were tried instead of the ring and did not work.
Adopted a publicly shared two-stage rectification pipeline (rotation/homography, then rectification) and predicted all leads from the rectified images.
The species classification head was trained with focal loss to handle the long-tailed class distribution.
Cross-validated by holding out each season from 2003 to 2025.
For natural-question play, the next question minimizes expected entropy over ~35,000 top-probability keywords, similar to another team's solution.
Pure transformer and other conv/transformer combinations did not work as well as Squeezeformer.

Rule-based fixes derived from OOF errors: drop non-title-case names, convert long phone numbers to ID_NUM, length filters for ID_NUM/URL, require @ in emails, fix USERNAME and address newline tokens. Described as key to CV/LB gains.

technique_name: Two-stage SFT: CoT then tool-integrated reasoning (MuMath-Code recipe)
technique_summary: Following MuMath-Code, stage 1 trains on chain-of-thought math solutions and stage 2 on tool-integrated reasoning traces (rationales, Python code, outputs), both full fine-tuning with LR 2e-5 and batch size 32.

technique_name: Event indicator as training feature, fixed at inference
technique_summary: Regressors were trained on all samples with efs as an input feature and evaluated on efs==1; at inference efs was set to 1. Adding the censored samples markedly improved the efs==1 ranking.
Models taking both SMILES and fingerprints as inputs did not work out.
EfficientNetV2-L for coordinate prediction and EfficientNetV2-S as a severity-model encoder, paired with ConvNeXt models.
A weighted random sampler built class-balanced training batches to counter class imbalance.
Each training stage used a stratified 5-fold split stratified on prompt_id combined with score.
An Albumentations pipeline with flips, transpose, affine (scale, translate, rotate, shear), blur, elastic/grid distortion, random resize-pad-crop and Gaussian noise was used.
Cancelled remaining generations once early answers agreed (e.g. 4 of first 5), and stopped after 10 of 12 completions to avoid stragglers.
The 128-patch baseline is fine-tuned at patch sizes 192 and 256 for 250 epochs; these fine-tuned models form most of both final ensembles.
Tournament selection was tried in place of diversity-based selection and did not work.
Predictions were smoothed over time with kernel [0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.2, 0.1].
Three GBDT types x 5 folds x 10 seeds gave 150 models; author says this added little over a 45-model setup but training was fast (under 20 minutes).
Four Transformer blocks over the 24x24 positions capture long-range spatial interactions; a small Transformer also forms the value head.
Two 4-model nnU-Net ensembles fuse softmax probabilities with fixed weights (0.12/0.28/0.18/0.42).
Used PyTorch 2.0 compile(), reported to give about a 1.5x speedup.
Final prediction blends two DINO-Large and two DINO-Base models with weights 0.4 and 0.6.
Continued iBOT pretraining of Phikon on 6.5M competition patches with 4 register tokens (one epoch, 2.5 days on 2 P100s); a submission mixing it scored well but was not selected for final evaluation.

technique_name: Gaussian noise on stacked model-prediction features
technique_summary: To counter image models overfitting the validation folds via early stopping, Gaussian noise (std 0.1, chosen by LB probing among several values) was added to prediction features during GBDT training.
AdamW with 1e-4 weight decay, LR 5e-4 to 1e-6, batch size 64.
LightGBM is used in both standard and DART boosting variants.

technique_name: Best-known packing methods such as sparrow
technique_summary: Untried future work; the author notes others quickly improved on the posted solution.

technique_name: Hill climbing / AutoGluon / CatBoost as ensembler
technique_summary: Hill climbing, AutoGluon and CatBoost as second-level ensemblers scored worse than Ridge.
EdgeNeXt-base (in21k_ft_in1k) was the second image architecture alongside EVA02-small.

technique_name: Stochastic skipping to flatten training data distribution
technique_summary: Ported nnue-pytorch dataloader skipping logic into a modified Primer tool to flatten the piece-count distribution and stochastically skip positions whose WDL likely matches the score.
Cross-validation groups by game_id with 5 folds, repeated three times with different splits.
Generated reasoning code runs in persistent Jupyter kernels that keep state, and execution results are fed back to refine solutions.

technique_name: Target differenced and normalized by installed capacity
technique_summary: The un-normalized differenced target and the raw target gave no benefit to the overall score and were dropped.
A simple mean ensemble scored CV 0.573; the author says the winning submission had public LB 0.578, but the text does not explicitly name which ensemble it was.
An unintended use of atomInSmiles produced an almost character-level tokenizer (atoms, digits, bracketed groups) with a 43-token vocabulary.
MLM pre-training used categorical focal cross-entropy with dynamic per-batch alpha weights; the author is unsure it contributed much.

technique_name: High-resolution neighbor matching with kNN-like ordering
technique_summary: A second transparent-scene approach estimates order from match counts in a kNN-like way and matches adjacent images at about 4096px; it scored reasonably, but its role in the final ensemble is not explicit.
Generated 64 raster candidate images per description with Segmind SSD-1B at 384x384 and guidance scale 8, as the basis for SVG conversion.
LightGBM with default parameters from a public notebook was one of three GBDT families, trained on GPU.
Both training stages used AdamW with a learning rate decaying linearly to zero.
AdamW optimizer with constant LR 1e-4 and weight decay 1e-3, trained with cross-entropy loss.
A soft head averages species traits weighted by classification softmax scores, addressing long-tail and inter-species correlation; it outperformed other heads.
ViT models such as EfficientViT performed significantly worse for this team.
A plain NN and TabM were trained as efs=0 classifiers and included among the classifiers combined with the GBDT regressors.
CLS and GeM pooling heads were used and varied across ensemble members.
Forward-selection ensembling improved public LB but worsened CV and private LB, so it was not relied on.

technique_name: Appending </s> special token to pull embedding similarity
technique_summary: In the Hugging Face sentence-t5, appending </s> pulls similarity toward about 0.9, but the host's TensorFlow scorer tokenizes it literally, motivating the lucrarea substitute.
Model predictions were converted to ranks and averaged, with minor weighting based on public LB and intuition.
An internal updater accumulated inferred hidden game parameters and observations over time (e.g. steps since a tile or enemy was last seen) to compute features.

technique_name: Regex-based PII predictions and span repair
technique_summary: As a final step, spans for NAME_STUDENT and ID_NUM were repaired and regex matches were added where models missed PII.
A custom 3D ConvNeXt predicts sagittal slice index; ConvNeXt-base is used for coordinate prediction and ConvNeXt-small as a severity encoder.
A LightAutoML MLP on the same 1,339 features and a simple 2-layer NN with skip connection on LGBM features are part of the ensemble.
To study the old/new data gap, models were trained on one subset and evaluated on the other, with a ranking-based oracle score; this analysis motivated the two-stage setup.

technique_name: Small ONNX model for efficiency track
technique_summary: A rushed efficiency solution with a half-layer DeBERTa xsmall exported to ONNX was still too slow.

The core matcher is the 3D foundation model MASt3R used as a semi-dense detector-free matcher (fast_reciprocal_NNs, size 512); the author found it far more precise than detector-based methods like ALIKED+LightGlue in messy scenes.
Column features are fed in three forms: per-level normalization, normalization over all levels, and a log-style transform, giving 1696 input features.
Short audio clips were padded by repeating them cyclically.
Uses the 20 frames before the pass with per-frame features: position, sin/cos of orientation, speed-scaled direction components, and offsets to the ball landing point and to the receiver.

technique_name: Island reset on stagnation or duplication
technique_summary: Islands are reinitialized when stuck for about 100 generations (unless best) or when their champion duplicates another island's champion.
Proposed as future direction, citing DeepSeek technical reports; not part of this solution.
Static features (12 dims) include one-hot player role, number of prediction frames, number of input frames, passer final position, ball landing point and player final position.
Qwen2 72B, fine-tuned with QLoRA on 5 folds, was the second teacher model for distillation.
Discussed nested CV as the leakage-free option for early stopping and selection, but judged it too expensive for about 150 OOFs.
A CatBoost regressor (CV 0.582) was one of the base models.
GLOMAP was tried in place of COLMAP together with pre-clustering but did not improve the score.

LightGBM models trained on anonymized external essay-scoring datasets (8 datasets, 24 essay types) with the same TF-IDF extractor predicted external scores, used as features; predictions correlated well with targets.

technique_name: Cosine similarity loss on trait vector
technique_summary: Treating the 6 traits as a vector, a cosine similarity term regularized the regression head to keep inter-trait correlations.

technique_name: Cfish (C port of Stockfish) as base engine
technique_summary: Started from Cfish, a C port of Stockfish, expecting a C codebase to be easier to shrink under the 64kb binary size limit than modern C++ Stockfish.
A Keras MLP is among the listed base models.
Patch features came from Phikon, a ViT-Base pathology foundation model pretrained with iBOT on 40M TCGA tiles; each slide becomes an (n_patches, 768) tensor.
Both GPUs are used to run SfM in parallel.
190 models' OOF predictions are stacked with Ridge regression (CV 8.56634 with post-processing).
A gated fusion of building-block representations did not work out as expected.
Per sheet, binary closing with a radius-3 sphere closes small holes and cavities.

technique_name: 72B AWQ model for second inference pass
technique_summary: Using quantized Qwen2.5-72B for the TTA pass only covered 5% of samples within budget and looked significantly worse on LB.

technique_name: Analysis of the data-generating simulator code
technique_summary: Key components (gain drift functional form, foreground handling) were derived by reading the ExoSim2/TauREx3 simulator code; the team says no leak was found but the solution partly exploits the simulator.
4-fold CV split by document id modulo 4, followed by one or two full-data fits; both fold and full-fit models were used in the ensemble.
Full low-res and high-res ClimSim data from Hugging Face (tens of millions of samples) were used; high-res mixed at 2:1 low:high with larger batches for stability.
Pseudo-labels in later iterations were raised to a power >1 (tuned per iteration on LB, e.g. 1/0.65, 1/0.55, 1/0.6) to suppress noise, which made multi-iteration self-training converge.
An eca_nfnet_l0 model from the 3rd self-training iteration, trained with extra Xeno-Canto target-species data, was in the final ensemble.
Many submissions, including the best-CV 4x large ensemble, used simple averaging to avoid overfitting weights.
ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B0 was the main backbone used directly without SED modifications.
EMA of weights gave a negligible change in score.

Raw-audio mixup was used in supervised training (p=0.5, left zero padding to guarantee overlap) and, in self-training, every labeled sample was mixed with a pseudo-labeled soundscape chunk at a fixed 0.5 weight.

technique_name: Align prediction shifts across fold models
technique_summary: Rank-loss (and GNN) predictions drifted between folds, hurting whole-set CV, so per-fold predictions were shifted to share the same mean/median.
Samples where teacher predictions disagreed most with human votes were manually reviewed to fix mislabeled pairs.

technique_name: Ensemble prediction variance for outlier detection
technique_summary: Using variance across Chowder ensemble members together with entropy to flag outliers was tried in a submission that was not selected for final evaluation.
378 features including key latency stats, activity/event counts, time to reach word counts, pause and revision-burst features, ratios, reconstructed-text stats and punctuation-error counts.
torch.compile roughly doubled inference speed, making high-resolution inference with TTA feasible.
Bootstrapping estimates the per-wavelength dip error, which varies with signal-to-noise, and these errors feed the Gaussian process.

technique_name: More generation candidates for harder problems
technique_summary: Problem difficulty was estimated from a Qwen2.5-72B-Math-Instruct pass rate, and harder problems received more solution candidates.
A random audio segment was sampled from each file instead of the first 5 seconds, improving over the baseline.

technique_name: Cancelling inverse moves at sequence junctions
technique_summary: When concatenating sequences, inverse moves at the end of one and start of the next cancel, shortening the total solution.
A variant interleaves the word NINE into a normal word list and places the score-9 injection in Korean (another variant uses Belarusian) to steer specific judges differently.
Cast every base feature to string and treated it as categorical (ALL_CATS feature set).
Retrieval CNNs were evaluated via frustum IoU against ground truth, but gains did not show on LB, so retrieval-based pair selection was abandoned.
A DeBERTa-v3-large ranking model trained with a pairwise margin loss.
Agent Alpha splits the candidate list by probability mass rather than by count, making the search more efficient.
DINOv3 backbone; Large and Huge performed similarly, so Large (and Base in the final pseudo-label stage) was used.
WSIs were tiled at 224 px and 40x TMAs at 448 px then resized to 224 px so all images are at roughly 20x; the notes say this gave consistent performance across test images.
Each model's predictions were converted to percentile ranks and averaged with equal weights.
The use_amp argument in MASt3R's inference function was fixed so automatic mixed precision is actually applied, as a speed optimization.
Question bank: 26 first-letter questions, ~3,000 from winning public games and ~10,000 generated by GPT-4o mini prompted with candidate keywords from simulated matches.

technique_name: Keep unscored class as extra training class
technique_summary: The unscored beta-amylase class was kept in training because it helps the model distinguish beta-galactosidase from it.
A denoising variational autoencoder's latent representation was used as a feature set (DVAE+ALL_CATS XGBoost was selected) to increase OOF diversity.

technique_name: Hold-out of building blocks for validation
technique_summary: Validation held out 3% of building blocks so validation molecules contained unseen blocks, about 9 million samples.
Instance-number models are trained as classification (CE over 32 slices) and regression (L1 on normalized x, y, z with x, y as auxiliary targets).
Candidate answers from SC-TIR traces were postprocessed and the final answer chosen by majority vote.

Training samples start prediction up to 20 frames before the pass, extending the target horizon, with a static feature for the offset (0 at test); reported to significantly improve long trajectories and reduce overfitting.
A NAME_STUDENT-only model (other labels set to O) did not work.
Teacher logits from Llama3 70B and Qwen2 72B were distilled into Gemma2-9B with a distillation loss among several losses (lr 5e-5); the author calls this the key part of the solution.
A critique model trained on 20k GPT-4o critiques was used to add CoT for teachers, but soft labels from critiques were consistently worse.

technique_name: Embedding prompt text hidden behind noise pattern
technique_summary: Embedded the stopword-stripped description as SVG path text covered by a repeating noise pattern, hiding it from OCR on the partially processed image but revealing it to aesthetic/VQA scoring.

technique_name: Height-partitioned feature head for four ECG rows
technique_summary: Three head variants: split backbone features by height into four row segments (strategies 1-2) or max-pool height and split channels into four (strategy 3), then expand to 4x input width.
Each question got 350s base time; unused time went to a shared buffer from which a question could draw up to 210 extra seconds.
Enforcing component-sum constraints or deriving some targets from others did not work.

technique_name: Parallel sampling of multiple generations per problem
technique_summary: Each problem launched 12 asynchronous generations with different seeds; reported accuracies use majority voting (maj@12).
SE-ResNeXt matched EfficientNet but was about 3x slower at inference, so it was not used.
Labels were normalized by summing expert votes per eeg_id, as part of the team's shared validation setup.

technique_name: Sigmoid activation at inference for CE-trained models
technique_summary: Although trained with softmax CE, models used sigmoid on logits at inference, a large gain over softmax in the step table.
Inspired by crowd-counting interval partition (UEPNet), auxiliary heads classify each target into intervals derived from training data; reported ~0.03 gain on LB and PB.

technique_name: Adding CLIP/VQA scores to selection criterion
technique_summary: Combining CLIP or VQA scores with aesthetic score for final selection did not improve scores.
Plays are flipped along the X-axis as an augmentation.
Additional weaker models such as tabular ResNet, FT-Transformer and field-aware factorization machines were built; whether they are in the final 190-model ensemble is not stated explicitly.
XGBoost was trained on many feature sets (BASE, TE, ALL_CATS, ORIG, DVAE) and several of these were frequently selected.
Boltz2 gives two predictions for short and mid-length sequences, with ligand SMILES included; skipped at 1000 nt or more to avoid OOM.
A BiLSTM layer before the classifier added ensemble diversity and smoother training; NaN losses were fixed by initializing the layer and saving with save_safetensors=False.
For globe puzzles, breadth-first search finds a setup sequence A placing three pieces where a base 3-rot R applies; A.R.-A yields a 3-rot for any three pieces.
Training used warmup over 15% of pre-training with cosine decay, 2 epochs, batch size 8, grad clip 10 and weight decay 0.01.
Deliberately pushed predictions at or beyond 97%/3% to 1/0, a gamble the author calls negative expected value but useful for finishing first.
Identical system/instruction prompt prefixes are cached and reused across parallel samples to improve throughput.
Post-hoc UMAP of averaged Phikon features revealed 38 WSIs likely saved at the wrong zoom (~x12); it also showed resized TMAs mix with WSIs. How this analysis affected training is not stated.

technique_name: Separate local validation per scene type
technique_summary: Local CV validated transparent and non-transparent scenes separately, using test-example and train scenes plus a 65-image pond subset, with COLMAP limited to one thread.
Teacher models see the generating model's name before each response, information not given to the student.

Final ensemble of 7 models from different self-training iterations, backbones and the dedicated group model; the chosen submission slightly upweighted B3 and NFNet, though equal weights scored best on private.
XGBoost is the second-best single model by CV and is among the tuned GBDTs feeding the ensemble.
DRFold2 cfg97 contributes one prediction for sequences under 250 nt, running fewer of its 20 models as length grows.
Heuristic rescaling (clover x0.8, dead scaled by magnitude) and blending of head outputs with component sums for GDM and total.
Severity models aggregate slice features with attention-based MIL, improving public LB from 0.37 to 0.35.
Women's top-4 seeds get a home advantage bump in the first two rounds, since they host those games.
All CNN models used a SED head adapted from the 4th place BirdCLEF 2021 solution, producing framewise predictions; it consistently beat other heads.
Kept the top 300 features by CatBoost importance to limit memory and allow more online-training rounds.

technique_name: Adding the prompt to the model input
technique_summary: Including the essay prompt in the model input did not work.

technique_name: LightAutoML tabular neural networks (DenseNet, ResNet, FT-Transformer)
technique_summary: LightAutoML tabular NNs (DenseNet, ResNet, FT-Transformer) complemented the tree models; mixing trees and NNs was considered important.

technique_name: Interpolate between noisy and re-estimated features
technique_summary: Nondeterministic provided features were recomputed 5 times for a less noisy estimate, and training values were sampled uniformly between that and the original; impact around 0.002 or less.
Fold0 trained better because it had lower signal statistics, so ensemble members were trained on fold0 and on subsets selected by the 0.8 quantile of T = std + var + rms + pwr instead of folds 0-4.
DeBERTa classifier trained with BCE on soft continuous labels, e.g. essays from instruction-tuned LLMs labeled below 1.
Opponents get 6/4/2/0.25 points by seed tier or secondary-tournament participation; summed over wins to form a quality-wins differential.
A second inference pass with swapped response order is run with the full-data model only on the 33% most uncertain samples.

technique_name: Repeating a small curated essay set with a chosen seed
technique_summary: The submission repeated a set of 15 crafted essays, later reduced to 12 after removing three judged impure, using random seed 1144 (one more than a seed shared publicly).
The winning submission used temperature 0 with greedy ReDrafter search, which still produced slightly varying outputs; chosen for stability and slightly faster speculative decoding.
Served the model with TensorRT-LLM engines using in-flight batching and paged KV caching.
LightGBM regressor and classifier were base models (CV 0.576 and 0.582) and LightGBM also produced the external-score features.
An EVA02-small bkl/melanoma/nevus classifier trained on ISIC archive data (diagnosis mapped by rules) supplied prediction features; it improved CV/LB and slightly improved the final model.
Stage 1: both student and teacher are fully fine-tuned with DeepSpeed ZeRO3 on public preference datasets (orpo-dpo-mix-40k, UltraFeedback-chinese) before task training.
Merging SFT and KTO models or SFT with public DeepSeekMath models via mergekit caused regressions or was not explored further.
The final transparent-scene ordering combines SSIM-based pair weights with a matching-based flow, reported as giving +0.09 on public LB.

technique_name: Synthetic positive images from a text-to-image model
technique_summary: Synthetic malignant lesion images (Derm-T2IM-like generation) improved individual model CV but did not help the final ensemble, so were excluded.
Special parts (e.g. cube corners) are solved first, then elementary moves make every remaining cluster an even permutation so 3-rots can finish them.
SED heads and a modified CNN from a BirdCLEF 2021 solution were slower and worse than plain backbones.

technique_name: Two-stage training: frozen backbone then full fine-tune
technique_summary: First trains fusion layers and heads with DINO frozen, then fine-tunes the whole model; chosen as most effective strategy.
A 4-layer Transformer encoder took the 200 stocks at a time step as the sequence and predicted all stocks jointly.
Turning off the public notebook's hot pixel (sigma clip) processing avoided losing central-pixel information needed to correct time-dependent PSF noise, giving a large LB gain.
The public-notebook trick of scaling predictions and clipping to a narrow range hurt LB when tuned on CV, so isotonic regression was used instead.
Relaxation uses an L-BFGS implementation adapted from PyTorch to work on batches, with cost and gradients computed directly in CUDA.
Test-time augmentation averaging did not help.
The submitted model was Qwen2.5-14B-Base supervised fine-tuned on 2.2M CoT solutions for 8 epochs with NeMo-Skills.
Each numeric base feature is duplicated as a categorical feature (in feature set 2, all base features after ordinal mapping).
South Carolina (women) and UConn (men) were made super teams that win every simulated game; the author notes this may have been more gambling than optimal.
Segmentation models were trained with mixed precision.

technique_name: Keyword prior from word frequency and LLM thing-ness
technique_summary: Each keyword's chance of being in the private list was estimated from word count, English word frequency and a GPT-4o mini 'thing-ness' Yes/No probability, calibrated against public keywords with smoothing.

technique_name: Horizontal king mirroring of input features
technique_summary: Mirrored the board horizontally so our king stays on one half, cutting king inputs by 32 for better compression and, per the author, stronger features relative to the king.
Keystroke-log features include latency and inter-key interval statistics, pause-duration counts, and a teammate feature reported to boost CV by 0.007+.
Training on the MMOS dataset improved results but capped at 16/50 public since it only produces single-turn programs; discarded.
On-policy KTO on 4 sampled completions per problem labelled by answer correctness improved internal evals and scored 27/50 public, but was not applied to the final model due to time.

technique_name: Other detectors and matchers (SP/SG, LoFTR, DKM, RoMa, etc.)
technique_summary: Many alternative detectors and matchers were tested, but ALIKED+LightGlue was best on LB; dense methods suffered from poor repeatability and noisy matches.
harry_Rating multiplies trimmed-mean season net efficiency by MinMax-scaled factors for schedule strength, power conference and (men) early AP top-12 status.
The three model stacks are blended with weights optimized on CV via Nelder-Mead.
TabICL run on 100k subsamples (x5) was a lower-CV but frequently selected ensemble member.
MSA inputs were enabled for RNAPro and RNA MSA for Protenix.
Each base model (CatBoost, LightGBM, TabM) is stacked with an isotonic regression model, and the stacks are then ensembled.
Five slices around the predicted instance are resized to 512x512 and cropped with condition- and plane-specific offsets around the predicted coordinates.
Training used a smoothed BCE loss combining three terms: main segmentation output, deep supervision, and a max-pooled loss.

technique_name: Final submission selection by CV-LB consistency
technique_summary: Observed CV-LB agreement broke above CV about 0.95578, so the final pick came from the 0.95578-0.95580 range rather than the highest-CV ensemble.
EfficientNet-B3 is the second encoder backbone used in the FlexibleUnet segmentation models.
A 29-feature subset was selected instead of the 25 features chosen in the reference notebook.
Duplicate training audio files were removed.
The 300 shared features were mostly common ones: raw and mid prices, imbalance features, rolling features and historical target features.
Final submission used nested CV of six bags by five folds stratified on score; the author trusted CV over LB.
Only sparse matching is used: an ensemble of ALIKED (n16, unlimited keypoints) extractors with tuned LightGlue matchers on high-resolution images.
All categorical features were one-hot encoded while the original categorical columns were also kept.
Two simple 2-layer GRU models took a 24-hour sequence of the 600 dense features plus six 16-dim categorical embeddings and output 24 hourly predictions; adding NNs improved the final score by 0.9.
A handful of plays with abnormal length or no passer are removed from training.
NN-style models were tried as regressors but did not work well, so only GBDTs were used as regressors.
Each image model's predictions were standardized independently before being fed to the GBDT.
From 1500 relaxed individuals per island, 27 lowest-overlap survivors are kept plus 84 chosen by low overlap subject to a minimum genetic distance from those already selected.
DeepSeek-Math, which writes Python programs, handled letter-counting and pattern questions about the keyword with high accuracy.

technique_name: Increasing RoPE base for long context
technique_summary: Raised the RoPE base to 500k so the model could handle long reasoning traces.
On Kaggle, applied x/y flip augmentation at inference, disabling it after 30 seconds of overtime to halve inference time and avoid timeouts.
Tomograms without any flagellar motor were removed from the training set.
Encoder was a 3D ResNet; ResNet101 for most experiments and ResNet200 in the final model since larger encoders performed better.
Final submission ensembles over 100 models of the same architecture, diversified by feature configurations and CV splits.
XGBoost with default parameters from a public notebook was one of three GBDT families in the ensemble.
A swish dense layer followed by a SwiGLU MLP block with head width 1024/2048 sits after the Squeezeformer blocks.
Adding 1D-CNN or MLP models to the ensemble did not help.

Logs were cleaned by dropping events more than ten minutes before first input, making up times start at zero and increase, capping gap/action times (10 and 5 minutes) and dropping Unidentified events.
Heads got higher learning rates with earlier warmup while backbone layers used scaled-down rates, balancing under- and overfitting during fine-tuning.
A bagging regressor (CV 0.594) was among the base models.
Besides Kaggle train data, an external 'ut' dataset and a 33k-sample dataset from competition discussions were used for post-pretraining and fold training.
Models used generalized-mean pooling over the frequency dimension before the SED head.
Removing dropout was tried for this regression task but was clearly worse, so dropout was kept.
Simply concatenating pseudo-labeled data into batches did not work, and a 5th self-training iteration gave no further improvement.
In the pseudo-label stage, no CV was used and an SWA of the final epochs was taken; extra train-only epochs reduced overfitting to pseudo-labels.
The exact separation distance between two trees is precomputed with Minkowski geometry into a 3D table (relative X, Y, angle) and queried with trilinear interpolation.
ConvNeXt V2 tiny and base backbones were among the ten ensembled models.
Five separate three-layer regression heads predict each biomass target without physical constraints during training.

Unlabeled soundscapes were pseudo-labeled by an ensemble of the Google classifier and the best train_audio models and used for training; Google-classifier pseudo labels were also added to train labels with weight 0.05.
Importance-based and iterative forward/backward feature selection did not work well.
5-fold training with 4/5 Kaggle train plus 33k data and 1/5 Kaggle train as dev; teachers produced out-of-fold probability distributions on the training set.
Larger Transformer architectures such as DeBERTa did not improve results.
Generating more than 64 candidate images was not adopted, though the authors note it seemed to work well on the private LB.
The writeup lists sample weighting as a model item but gives no details on how weights were defined or used.
