Additional filters removed positions from the first 28 plies and kept positions where a piece sacrifice is the best move; filtered passes were stacked to mimic multiple stochastic traversals.
Final submission ensembled 8 seeds by summing sigmoid outputs; inference took about 10 hours.
Scaled rewards with a multiplier computed from a sliding average of returns so value targets stayed within roughly [-5, +5] throughout training.
Added per-feature value frequency counts, used e.g. in a selected LightGBM feature set.
Human texts came from the full PERSUADE corpus plus GPT-2 output dataset, ELLIPSE, NarrativeQA, Wikipedia, Brown corpus and IMDB reviews.

technique_name: Merge multiple reconstructions via Horn alignment
technique_summary: When COLMAP returns several models, Horn alignment estimates transforms and projects other models into the best one to register more images.
Five fold-wise Qwen2.5-72B teachers produce out-of-fold soft labels; the 14B student is distilled with weighted CE, KL and cosine losses.
vLLM served batched sampling of N candidates per problem during SC-TIR inference.

technique_name: Dedicated model for underrepresented species groups
technique_summary: An EfficientNet-B0 trained on 700 Amphibia/Insecta species (40 epochs, BS 128) had its target-species predictions inserted into a zero matrix for ensembling, adding about 0.002-0.003 LB.

technique_name: Downscaled image placement in composed SVG
technique_summary: The vectorized image was scaled to 40% and placed at the top center, leaving room for the embedded text and artifacts.
Gaussian process, autoencoder and NMF predictions are blended 6:2:2; each alone scored clearly below the blend in late-submission ablations.
A lowercase, special-character-stripped version of the data was made to diversify the ensemble and resist character attacks; its contribution to the final ensemble is not quantified.
Generated blank ECG images so the model learns not to output spurious values under occlusion/noise, and randomly varied ground-truth signals.

technique_name: Re-running training to exploit run-to-run variance
technique_summary: Because identical configs produced networks of varying strength, repeating training from scratch several times yielded stronger networks; the selection procedure is not detailed.
When aggregating windows via roi_weight_map, the central 40% of each window was weighted 1.0 and the edges 0.001.

technique_name: Predicting target bucket mean with GBDT
technique_summary: Using GBDT to predict the target bucket mean did not work.
Answer probabilities from the three LLMs were averaged to form the final table.
Tissue regions were found by Otsu thresholding on the slide thumbnail in HSV color space before tiling.
Using the FGS1 channel was listed as future work if more time were available.

technique_name: Sliding-window chunked inference for long sequences
technique_summary: Long sequences are split into 512-nt windows with 128 overlap, folded independently by Protenix and stitched by C1' coordinates, later chunks overwriting overlaps.
All submitted models were retrained on all data, so they differed somewhat from OOF models; seed averaging helped stabilize this.

technique_name: Averaging aesthetic score over repeated processing
technique_summary: Averaging aesthetic scores across multiple runs of the image processing pipeline did not improve results.
Hyperparameters were searched with Optuna using 5-fold single-seed CV, then candidates were re-checked with 10-fold CV and 3 seeds.

Added a colored-square patch (four variants tested per image) and several short text strings, found by genetic algorithm, hill climbing or manual search, to raise the aesthetic score without lowering VQA.
An initial jiggling step on solutions was tried and listed among things that did not work.
Split generation over both T4 GPUs (32 images each); single-threading was used for reliability, taking about 30 seconds for 64 images.
The winning model is a small Transformer encoder trained from scratch on SMILES: 4 layers, 8 heads, key/value dimension 32, built in TensorFlow/Keras.

technique_name: Task post-pretraining on external data before fine-tuning
technique_summary: All three base models were first trained one epoch on the ut dataset (lr 1e-5), and these weights initialized the subsequent fold training.
Actions and iterations per second measured during the starting-position search were added as less noisy speed features; they helped CV but had no clear LB effect.

technique_name: DPM-Solver multistep scheduler with few steps
technique_summary: Used a DPM-Solver multistep scheduler with only 12 inference steps for efficiency.
CountVectorizer token-count features used in the LGBM feature set.
Very deep gradient-boosted tree configurations did not improve CV.
An initial approach based on KenPom, Massey ordinals and 538 data was abandoned because 538 was unavailable for 2025 and Massey data arrived late.

technique_name: Tiny AutoEncoder (TAESDXL) in place of default VAE
technique_summary: Replaced the default VAE with the tiny TAESDXL autoencoder to speed up image generation.
Final CoT weights were obtained by averaging checkpoints from different stages of training; the TIR model used the last checkpoint without averaging.
The three head outputs were blended with learnable weights to produce final traits.
Inference runs along all three axes with 8x test-time augmentation.
Cosine learning-rate schedule with peak LR 0.001 and effective batch size 32.

technique_name: Forcing Agent Alpha mode without asking
technique_summary: Skipping the handshake question and forcing Agent Alpha to save a turn is mentioned as possibly viable in hindsight.
No external data was used; the author relied on augmentation, loss design and architecture to compensate for the limited dataset.
N-gram features on non-space characters of the reconstructed essay.
Fusing logits instead of probabilities was not chosen based on public LB, though the authors note it was better on private LB.
43 features that differed from the organizer's values (suspected Ludii version mismatch) were dropped together, consistently improving CV by 0.001-0.002.
Float regression outputs are cut into integer scores with thresholds optimized for QWK via Powell minimization of 1-QWK, averaged over 15 starting points and 3 seeds.
Image model batches were balanced 1:1 between classes to address extreme class imbalance.
Computed target mean, smoothed target mean, weight of evidence and entropy from the original dataset as external target-encoding-style features.
The Google bird-vocalization classifier filtered train chunks: chunks whose top prediction did not match the primary label were dropped, and labels were swapped when it matched a secondary label.

technique_name: Sample noisy features from repeated search runs
technique_summary: Tree-search features were computed 10 times and training rows randomly draw values from the 9 non-held-out runs, exposing models to feature noise; about +0.002 CV and LB.

technique_name: Concatenating generated predictions from multiple LLMs
technique_summary: Outputs of all models were concatenated into a single predicted prompt string as an ensemble.
Listed under what didn't work: training and inference with stride.
Candidate subqueries retrieving identical target sets are deduplicated to shrink the annealing search space.
Boltz2 generates 10 diffusion samples per target and keeps the 5 best by pLDDT plus confidence score.

technique_name: Keyword-question answer probability table from LLM Yes/No logits
technique_summary: p(Yes | keyword, question) for every pair (about 35,000 x 13,000) was estimated from next-token Yes/No likelihoods of Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Phi-3-small and gemma-7b-it.
DeepTables neural model is listed among the main base models.
3D models were listed under what did not work.
A custom loss with weight 1.0, inspired by a forum post and a public fast surface-dice metric implementation, is included in training.

technique_name: Alternative pathology feature extractors (CTransPath, LUNIT, DinoV2)
technique_summary: CTransPath, LUNIT and DinoV2 backbones were benchmarked but underperformed Phikon in CV and did not help in ensembles; they were not in the winning submission (one other selected submission used CTransPath and LUNIT).
Models were trained as regressors with MSE or BCE on targets scaled to [0, 1], and the loss was varied for ensemble diversity.
Placing the colored-square patches elsewhere (along the border, left of the image, etc.) did not improve scores.
Llama3 70B was trained with QLoRA on 5 folds as a teacher to produce logit distributions for distillation.
Targets zeroed in submission or replaced by the ptend trick were excluded from the loss.
RNAPro refines from TBM templates with MSA and RibonanzaNet2 embeddings, giving 2 predictions for 250-999 nt and 1 for short sequences.

technique_name: Reconstruct final essay text from keystroke logs
technique_summary: Essay text was reconstructed from keystrokes, improved with nearest fuzzy-match search and Undo correction when cursor/text-change info mismatched; 142 events still had errors.
Each image was downsampled, quantized to six colors, and converted to simplified OpenCV contour polygons rendered as compressed SVG paths.
Both orderings of the two responses are included in the same gradient step during training.
Cosine learning-rate schedule starting from 1e-4.
Ranking loss using crop-vs-full and label-based inter-image orderings improved CV but hurt LB, likely overfitting.

technique_name: Validation on external competition math benchmark
technique_summary: Local validation used a 256-problem set from AIME 2024/2025 and HMMT 2024/2025; private LB later tracked this CV better than public LB.
RGF had lower standalone CV but was frequently selected in ensemble search for its complementary errors.
Models fit on external essay datasets (FB2, FB3, AES, IELTS) with letters masked to 'q' produce predictions used as features, giving a 0.008 boost.
Using depth masks and RANSAC on a bird's-eye x,z projection to remove wrong matches in symmetric scenes was listed among ideas that did not work out.
OpenFE automated feature generation did not work well.
Character-level TF-IDF features on reconstructed essays boosted CV by ~0.005; word n-gram TF-IDF also fed a Ridge model.
Various semi-supervised methods were implemented and tuned but did not beat direct hard pseudo-labeling.
K-means clustering was listed among things that did not work.
A supervised auxiliary head predicted next-tick enemy positions, adjacency and sensor masks with weighted BCE from partial ground truth; its output fed the action head and the next step's input.
An NMS strategy from an IMC2023 team improved the church scene locally but did not help on LB.
Albumentations-style flips, RandomRotate90, Gaussian noise, brightness/contrast, HSV shift, CLAHE and color jitter, applied independently to each sub-image.
Since 7z gave the best ratio and was available in the competition container, the engine binary was 7z-compressed and unpacked at runtime, with zopfli for the outer archive.
Coordinate predictions from ConvNeXt-base and EfficientNetV2-L are averaged.
Aggregated statistics computed over sentences and paragraphs of the reconstructed essay; a double-newline paragraph-split variant gave +0.001.
Down-weighting low-confidence predictions in the ensemble showed no promising results in brief late experiments.
Components under 20K voxels are removed; in the authors' cumulative table this step raised private score from .596 to .614.
XGBoost was used both as an efs=0 classifier and as an efs_time regressor; it gave the best regressor c-index on efs==1 in the reported table.
Queries use only AND and OR; terms are joined with hyphens to drop explicit AND tokens, with cpc terms placed last since they cannot be hyphen-joined.

Teachers train on lmarena human-preference-55k plus competition data (filtered and deduplicated to 80k); distillation adds further public arena datasets including PPE-Human-Preference-V1 and nbroad's datasets.
12-block Squeezeformer models (dim 256/384/512) adapted from the Ribonanza 2nd-place solution, with an ECA layer added and first LayerNorm removed in the conv block.
The regression head used R2 loss on normalized traits, and the blended output used R2 loss on unnormalized traits so gradients reach all heads; loss weights were tuned manually.
Random brightness/contrast applied after cropping with p=0.25.
The middle 10,000 frames of each EEG recording were cropped for validation, following the referenced starter method.
cp.intersect1d made intersections 2-3x faster than Python sets, allowing all cpc/title/abstract words; author credits this with moving from 3rd to 1st.
Recommended for parallel hyperparameter tuning, but the author says they never tried it.
Mistral was trained with (Q)LoRA (rank 64, alpha 16, dropout 0.1) on attention projection modules.
Observations and actions of the second player were flipped so the agent always sees itself starting at (0, 0).
Bootstrapped TIR data from a LIMO-finetuned instruction model with iterative training, generation and filtering to 1.7M solutions, then filtered to 15K by code-execution count and correctness.
Weighting the loss per output frame was tried and gave no meaningful improvement.

technique_name: Multiply spectrum by a constant coefficient
technique_summary: Other teams scaled the final spectrum by about 1.006-1.008; the authors' ablation shows this was worse than proper foreground processing.
Training used 10 s inputs from two adjacent 5 s chunks with averaged labels to capture full chirp periods; at inference each 5 s chunk is predicted with 2.5 s of context on each side.

technique_name: Split label mass between primary and secondary labels
technique_summary: For files with secondary labels, the primary label gets 0.5 and the other 0.5 is split evenly among secondary labels.
Essays end with an injected instruction telling the judge to ignore prior instructions and output a score of 9; listed as one of several alternative attack sets.
CatBoost was the strongest single model in the final blend (reported CV 5.8240, private 5.4165 with online learning and post-processing).
DRFold2 candidate structures are ranked by a MAD-normalized geometric energy score and the top-5 kept.

Because CV was unstable across split strategies, the same 10-fold StratifiedKFold split (stratified on a combined target key, fixed seed) was used for all classifiers and regressors to keep results comparable.

technique_name: Predict displacement from last observed position
technique_summary: The target is the displacement relative to the final input frame; the trajectory is reconstructed by adding predicted displacements to the last coordinates.
The solution ensembles CatBoost, LightGBM and the DenseLight network; exact ensemble weights are not given in the text.
Pseudo-labeling train_audio with a high coefficient noticeably hurt, and pseudo labeling with softmax temperature gave negligible change.
Feature set 2 (best for GBDTs) ordinally maps categorical features following a public notebook.

technique_name: Square size as optimized parameter (inward squeeze)
technique_summary: Including square size in the cost to create an inward squeezing force did not work in the GA, though the idea is reused in the legalize step.
LightAutoML DenseLight network on 865 features from a public sentence/paragraph feature notebook.
Rating differences are converted to a predicted point margin and then to a win probability via a normal CDF.
Targets were Gaussian heatmaps around each motor at 8x reduced resolution, justified by the metric's large distance tolerance.
A single regression head was insufficient, so the model used three heads (regression, species classification, soft classification) on a shared backbone.

Two rounds of pseudo-labelling relabelled old essays with new-style float scores (first round averaged with original score, second round predictions only); the chosen best submission mixed 1st and 2nd round models.
Test-time online training: four diverse models pseudo-label the test set, DINO-Large models train on train+test, then a second pseudo-label round trains DINO-Base models; reported >0.02 gain.
Used 4-fold CV, which correlated with LB up to about 0.93; beyond that the public LB (with quantile thresholding) was used for validation.
Each 2x2x2 neighborhood is made 6-connected watertight via a 256-entry lookup table, inspired by Euler-number computation.
Matches are fed to a general COLMAP reconstruction pipeline based on the public IMC25 baseline submission notebook, using COLMAP's multiple reconstructions instead of pre-clustering.
Rank-5 NMF reconstructs spectra for ensemble diversity; its components align with CO2, CH4 and H2O absorption.

technique_name: Filtering generated solutions by answer verification
technique_summary: Incorrect generated solutions were removed by an LLM judge checking answer equivalence; when no reference answer existed, the majority candidate answer was used.
Image models trained up to 200 epochs with early stopping after 10 validation checks without improvement; most stopped before 100 epochs.
Pre-training on the larger ZINC dataset was explored for about a month but did not work out as expected.
Doppelgangers and Yan et al. disambiguation methods were tried; Yan gave a tiny CV gain but an LB drop, so both were skipped.

technique_name: Random 3D volume rotation for oblique slices
technique_summary: The volume is randomly rotated in 3D so slices are not axis-aligned; a model trained this way for 30 epochs was in the ensemble and was also the best single private-LB model.
Other autoencoder variants were listed among methods that did not improve CV.
Generated nonlinear interaction features with gplearn mainly to add ensemble diversity; a RealMLP on GP features was among selected models.
Image order around the object is found by building a pairwise distance matrix and solving a Travelling Salesman Problem.
Cross-validation used a shuffled GroupKFold grouped by ruleset name.
PCA and other metadata consolidation approaches were tried and failed before switching to self-attention.
The provided trait SD data was not useful for predicting mean species traits.
TF-IDF features were built on activities, events, categorized latencies, and word/char n-grams of the reconstructed text.
Adding synthetic shadows to training images was listed as not working.

technique_name: Loss weighted by competition metric weights
technique_summary: Each target's loss term is scaled by the competition's weighted-R^2 target weights.
AutoGluon on the base+bin+digit+categorical set had the best representative single-model OOF AUC listed.
Not used: serving an extra generative reranker cost memory and time, and larger batch size and max tokens were a simpler alternative.
MLM pretraining of the small DeBERTa on train plus test essays before classification fine-tuning.
With probability 0.5 the whole play is rotated around the mean player position by a uniform 0-360 degree angle; the author reports it helps reduce overfitting.
Rounding predictions to the score grid never worked.
Feeding multiple days instead of a single day into the GRU did not work.
Augmented the competition tomograms with external tomograms from the CryoET Data Portal.
ftfy was used to fix unicode errors in event and text-change columns, reducing the number of unseen test up/down events.
Ensemble weights were also fitted with Nelder-Mead and hill climbing; two of the three final submissions used fitted (including negative) weights.
Data stored in FP64, downcast to FP32 for the model, and predictions upcast to FP64 before de-normalization.
Given as the reason for the custom plugging function: dilation adds too many voxels and can hurt the dice score.
RealMLP was the strongest single model (CV 8.58742 in the table); the author notes the best single model would have placed 7th.
Enforcing monotonic constraints in CatBoost did not work well.

technique_name: Extra no-call class from external data
technique_summary: An extra nocall class gave no public improvement and was not used, though the authors later observed a private score increase.
Coarse-to-fine matching did not work, which the author attributes to a probable implementation bug.
Statistics computed over 60 fixed 30-second time intervals instead of over pause gaps.

technique_name: Elo ratings and mixed effects models
technique_summary: The author previously used Elo ratings and mixed effects models but did not use them this year.
For validating the transparent-scene approach, the team recorded their own dataset of plastic and glass bottles.
Random brightness/contrast augmentation is part of the training augmentation pipeline.
The backbone is nnU-Net, starting from a public training notebook; the baseline uses patch size 128, batch size 2 and 4000 epochs.
Used sequence packing and context parallelization from NeMo-Aligner to speed up training on long reasoning data; training ran 48 hours on 512 H100s.
XGBoost and GRU predictions were combined, giving better validation and test MAE than either model alone in the reported table.

technique_name: Fallback text-only SVG on timeout or error
technique_summary: Prepared a text-only fallback SVG with decoy text, description text and some artifacts; the authors say their best submissions did not actually use it.
A normal essay is followed by bracket-closing junk and an instruction conditioned on the judge model's identity (or on understanding Base64) to assign different scores per judge.

technique_name: Stronger models trained on hard problems
technique_summary: Stronger models trained on hard problems produced more tokens, and the team was not confident they would finish within Kaggle time limits, so they were not submitted.
Longformer and LLM models did not work; causal-LM inference was too slow.

technique_name: Propagating a predicted name to all identical tokens in a document
technique_summary: Any token predicted as NAME_STUDENT causes every identical token in the same document to be labeled NAME_STUDENT.
Per-problem compute budget with dynamic redistribution of unused time; near the time limit sampling and verification are cut back and best partial outputs returned.
Questions containing trigger words such as 'letter' were routed to DeepSeek-Math, others to Llama-3.
Because competition labels were noisy, missing motors were manually annotated using Napari; the updated data was shared as an external dataset.
RLOO with code execution feedback and a binary correctness reward gave no significant gains and was slow, so RL was abandoned for KTO.
Answers from parallel samples are aggregated with weights from token-level Shannon entropy (lower entropy = higher confidence) instead of plain majority vote.
Two-stage training: stage 1 on Stockfish-generated data scored by low-node search, then stage 2 resumed from that checkpoint on lc0 data, which beat training on the strongest data from scratch.

technique_name: Best-of-N selection by proxy aesthetic score
technique_summary: Rendered and processed every candidate SVG and submitted the one with the highest aesthetic score (about 0.563 aesthetic and 0.88 VQA on validation).
Listed under unsuccessful experiments: forcing similar pre-head embeddings for both response orders to remove order bias and the need for a second pass.
Yandex's TabM, with piecewise linear embeddings, wide hidden layers, small batches and low LR, was the best single CV model and competitive with LightGBM on LB.
Inference used OpenVINO without quantization, multiprocess soundscape loading, and spectrograms computed once and shared across models.

technique_name: Unit-centered patch extraction for action heads
technique_summary: For each of 16 units a 15x15 patch centered on the unit is cut from the shared features, combined with per-unit features via a small MLP, then fed to movement and sap heads.

technique_name: Restricting in-memory index to test-relevant patents
technique_summary: Only patents in test.csv and their words are loaded to cut memory use.
Offspring are produced by one mutation (move, jiggle in four variants, twist, translate with wrap-around) or by crossover, enlarging each island population to 3750.
Input duration experiments (5-30 s) showed 20 s chunks best on public LB, attributed to long repetitive amphibian/insect calls; chunks were absmax-normalized and hop length scaled accordingly.
CatBoost was tried and tuned but performed worse than XGBoost.
Training ran up to 30 epochs with early stopping on validation balanced accuracy, patience 4.
Per-label decision thresholds were used instead of one global threshold across the 13 PII labels.
Separate learning rates for torso and head appear in the best params, but the author rates the effect as only a tiny difference.
Optuna tuned group weights and the voting threshold on out-of-fold predictions.
Predictions below 85% were boosted by 10% for both men's and women's games as a deliberate risk-taking adjustment.
Splitting images into multiple crops to find similar images for pair selection was listed among ideas that did not work out or were not fully tested.

technique_name: Pruning unnecessary engine code to reduce binary size
technique_summary: Removed unneeded engine components such as tablebase code and the original 2020 NNUE implementation to fit the size limit, then ported selected search patches from Stockfish history.

technique_name: Self-generated extra game rulesets and labels
technique_summary: Extra rulesets were generated (mostly via a GAVEL reimplementation) and annotated with cheap 4-match agent pairings; despite noisy labels this improved about 0.004 CV and 0.001-0.002 LB.
Fixed probability thresholds for motor presence were found unstable and replaced by quantile thresholding.

technique_name: Ensemble of MCTS algorithms for starting evals
technique_summary: Combining several MCTS algorithms for starting-position evals seemed at best equivalent to running one algorithm longer.

technique_name: Soft clipping of features and targets
technique_summary: Extreme normalized features are softly clipped (square-root then log style beyond cutoffs), and high-res targets are soft-clipped relative to low-res target ranges.
Horizontal flips (with vertical flips and transpose) are applied during training.

technique_name: Filtering ensemble members by held-out performance
technique_summary: After calibration, only a subset of the 50 Chowder models per ensemble was kept, selected by calibrated performance on the internal CV test fold.
TTA with length 2000 was applied at submission, improving LB loss from 0.882 to 0.876.
The backbone applies 24 residual blocks to a 24x24x128 encoded feature map.
Both final models use a ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone in a 2.5D setup with 3 input channels at 3x1536x1536.
RealMLP models on several feature sets were among the strongest single models and were selected in the ensemble.

technique_name: Adaptive entropy coefficient with decaying target entropy
technique_summary: Each action head had a target entropy (e.g. 0.9 movement, 3.9 sap) decaying linearly to 0 over 100M steps, with the coefficient auto-adjusted; targets were reset lower for continued training.
Experience was generated by self-play against the latest agent in some fraction of games, with other games against frozen older models or a teacher.
Applying the pixel-wise loss on lower-level decoder outputs (deep supervision) was found to give little gain; whether it was kept is not stated.

technique_name: Stacking more than 3 slices for 2.5D input
technique_summary: Using more than three stacked slices as 2.5D input did not work.

technique_name: Section crossover with island mate selection
technique_summary: Mates come from the same island or from lower-scoring champions of nearby ring islands, protecting young islands; the restriction lifts when an island stalls.
Core training was large-scale multi-agent IMPALA with V-trace, plus UPGO, TD losses and an entropy term.
Other augmentations including mixup, noise, pixdrop, blur, 1D audio augmentations and horizontal flip noticeably decreased the score.
Splitting into separate models by is_business did not work.
Bi-/tri-gram and proper atomInSmiles tokenization did not work out as expected.
XGBoost (reg:squarederror objective, gbtree, lossguide growth, 704 rounds) was the final model, building on raddar's public notebook.
Expanding high-order feature interactions did not improve CV.
Trained the small networks with the bullet trainer; the author states data selection and processing mattered most for network strength.
The author deliberately trained without early stopping to reduce overfitting risk, especially given the large number of folds.
Matches TTA: matches from multiple resolutions (1280 and 2048) on both original and cropped images are combined.
A bidirectional LSTM over slice features before attention MIL, together with auxiliary losses and ensembling, improved public LB from 0.35 to 0.33.
Validation used 5-fold stratified group k-fold (stratified and grouped), shared by GBDT and image models.
Auxiliary GaussianNLL losses on velocity and acceleration (first and second differences of predicted xy) stabilize and accelerate learning.
Generation used contrastive search, guidance scale, typical_p, high temperature/top-k, fill-in-the-blank, rewriting and prompting with or without source texts.

Following a publicly shared idea, predictions for earlier estimated periods were reduced by a constant; the author chose the split at 1/2 and a 0.03 reduction as a neutral bet, applied in the second selected submission.
A public community-shared coordinate dataset was used to pretrain the coordinate prediction models.
OmniGlue merged with ALIKED+LG gave the best private score but no noticeable public LB gain, so it was not in a selected submission.
SmoothL1 loss was compared and replaced by GaussianNLLLoss, which performed better.
Additional 4000-epoch models were trained from scratch at patch sizes 160, 192 and 224; only the 192-patch one entered the final ensemble (Set 2).
Because full validation was slower than an epoch, validation ran every 5 epochs early and gradually more often until every epoch by epoch 50.
vLLM was used to compute the large probability table, scaling from one 4090 to a rented 8x RTX 4090 node (about $500 reported).
Added aggregation features computed within groups of seconds_in_bucket, such as ratios of first values and rolling means to current values.
Vahadane and Reinhard color normalization were tried to address inter-center variability but gave no improvement.
The guesser first asks whether the answerer supports Agent Alpha mode (a shared binary-search protocol), falling back to natural questions otherwise.
Before cropping, coordinates are shifted by up to 10 px and slice index by up to 2 with probabilities matching stage-1 error rates, making stage 2 robust to localization errors.
Generating extra unlabeled data and using external datasets was listed as not working.
The public-notebook stacking approach using OOF predictions as features did not work well.

technique_name: Duplicate continuous features as categorical features
technique_summary: Continuous features were additionally copied into categorical versions as extra inputs.

technique_name: Left/right image split through shared backbone
technique_summary: Each image is split into left and right halves that pass through the same backbone, following popular public notebooks.
Per-class thresholds tuned by grid search each epoch, then recalibrated on OOF predictions by fitting each fold's threshold on the other 6 folds and averaging the F4 curves.
Models were implemented in TensorFlow and trained on Kaggle/Colab TPUs from TFRecords, with inference on a Kaggle P100.

technique_name: Per-model thresholds combined with ensemble weights
technique_summary: To limit overfitting with only 4.5k samples, thresholds were fit per model and combined using the same ensemble weights rather than fitted jointly.
GBDT training kept the public notebook's oversampling of the minority (malignant) class.
Final submission is a weighted ensemble of 8 models (with an intercept), with weights fit using shared out-of-fold predictions.
Ensemble members' predictions are combined by simple averaging.

technique_name: Language model predicting balance from rules
technique_summary: Training language models to predict game balance from Ludii rule text did not yield accurate results.
Used gradient checkpointing to reduce GPU memory use when training on large 3D volumes.

technique_name: Masked loss for partially labeled targets
technique_summary: Loss and metrics were masked because the external data only had labels for the sEH protein target.
Rotation angles from a Gaussian with sigma 5 degrees were used first, but larger variance performed better, so it was replaced by uniform sampling.
Static KV cache plus torch compilation gave 2-3x speedup on H100 but failed on Kaggle T4s, mainly due to lack of sharding support with compilation.
DeBERTa-v3-large used as a classifier and as a ranking model; a DeBERTa-v3-small with custom tokenizer was also trained.
Training used batch size 8 with 4 gradient accumulation steps.
During self-training, drop_path_rate 0.15 was applied to all models as Noisy Student noise, giving LB gains up to 0.005 for some models.
8-bit KV cache allowed longer contexts, more stable VRAM use and more parallel generations.
LightGBM was weaker than CatBoost alone but helped in the ensemble.
An exponential moving average of model weights with decay 0.9995 is used during training.
Final prediction blended CatBoost, GRU and Transformer with weights 0.5/0.3/0.2 tuned on the validation set.
All cpc, title and abstract words are kept, while claim and description words appearing 100,000+ times are dropped.
Images are min-max scaled to [0,1], sorted by DICOM metadata and padded to depth 32; coordinate labels are normalized by width, height and depth.
Stochastic depth gave no improvement in the purely supervised stage.
The five submitted structures are assigned to models by length tier (<250, 250-999, 1000+), tuned empirically and for runtime, to maximize best-of-5 diversity.
Plays moving left are rotated by 180 degrees so all plays share a common direction.
Axial slice indices are computed with a public 2D-to-3D DICOM projection method rather than a learned model.
A separate auxiliary attention score over slices is trained directly with cross-entropy as an auxiliary loss.

Each offspring is relaxed to a local minimum of a cost combining pairwise tree overlap and out-of-boundary penalties; zero cost means a feasible packing. Reported to run 30,000 times per second for 100 trees on an RTX 5090.
Patch inputs at multiple resolutions gave decent but unstable CV and poor LB/PB.
De-blurring images affected by camera shake was tried but gave no noticeable LB improvement.
The 3D ResNet200 encoder was initialized from pretrained weights from the 3D-ResNets-PyTorch repository.
A ConvLSTM with a 24x24x128 hidden state follows the residual blocks to give the agent memory across timesteps.
All team members used the same stratified k-fold split on the score so OOF predictions could be combined for ensemble weighting.
Training one model per biomass target and merging was listed among ideas that did not work.
Training used AdamW with a cosine annealing LR schedule, initial LR 1e-3 to 3e-3, 7-12 epochs, batch size 96.
Pretraining image models on earlier ISIC competition data and other ISIC archive sources gave no significant improvement.
Models were trained on all available data rather than holding out folds.
Emphasizing recent-season performance was listed under what did not work well.
AMC (83 integer-answer problems), AIME 22-24, and MATH level 4/5 integer subsets (~750 each) guided model and hyperparameter selection, with multi-seed runs to measure variance.
Wrapped the description in a flat clip-art style prompt and used a negative prompt against realism, gradients, texture and thin lines to get images that vectorize well.
One run swapped first and last names in some essays to handle names that can be either B- or I-NAME_STUDENT; whether it entered the final ensemble is not stated.

technique_name: Grayscale input concatenated with coordinate channels
technique_summary: Converted cropped images to grayscale and added coordinate-based feature channels to give the network spatial context.

technique_name: Replace BatchNorm/ReLU with GroupNorm/GELU plus extra conv stem
technique_summary: The U-Net was modified by swapping BatchNorm and ReLU for GroupNorm and GELU and adding an extra convolutional stem.
Reverse-engineered the hidden time order: the gap between date_decision and min_refreshdate_3813885D correlated strongly with WEEK_NUM, enabling the metric hack.

technique_name: Zeroing unused network weights for compressibility
technique_summary: Instead of removing impossible inputs (e.g. pawns on first/last rank), the unused weights were set to zero, improving compression of the submission without extra code.

technique_name: Median ensembling of classification and regression outputs
technique_summary: Slice-index predictions from 5-fold classification and regression models are combined by median per level.

Each wavelength's dip is fit with star spectrum x box transit x (1 + f(t) g(lambda)), using ExoSim2's separable gain-drift form with 5-parameter polynomials f and g; spectrum and dip are solved analytically.
A U-Net architecture was listed among what did not work.
The author states other competitors exploited leaks while this solution did not, and published a full reproducible pipeline to show it.

technique_name: Factorized movement and sap-target action heads
technique_summary: Per unit, one head picks among 6 actions (stay, 4 moves, sap) and a second head picks the sap tile in a 15x15 window, trained only on steps where sap was chosen.
A larger threshold (0.35-0.4, best on the training set) was not submitted after trusting public LB, although it was better on private LB per the authors.
Predictions were clipped to the valid score range 0.5-6.0.

A scikit-learn Gaussian process regressor with an RBF plus Matern kernel smooths the dip spectrum across wavelengths, using bootstrap errors as per-point uncertainty; it was the strongest single component.
Stage 1 predicts slice instance numbers and in-plane coordinates for each spinal level to build test coordinates; stage 2 predicts severity from crops around them.
Per-period (monthly, weekly) statistics of income, expenditure and tax did not help.
Larger encoders performed worse: convnext-large < convnext-base < convnext-small in the author's experiments.
Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct is the final student/base model; Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct is used as the teacher.
For the final two submissions, increased the optimum time allocation factor from the long-standing +1/4x default to +1/3x and +2/5x.

technique_name: Ranked path selection under SVG byte budget
technique_summary: Paths were ranked by size, centrality and simplicity and added until the 6000-byte limit, taking about 2.5 seconds per batch of 64.

technique_name: Eliciting TIR from a reasoning model by prompting alone
technique_summary: Simply prompting DeepSeek-R1 to produce tool-integrated solutions did not work; the authors hypothesize such models resist changing their solution format.
Secondary labels were treated as full positives in the targets.

technique_name: Padding essays with tokens from a judge model's vocabulary
technique_summary: One attack variant prefixes a list of token fragments taken from Qwen's vocabulary before an injected scoring instruction; the author notes a single comma mattered. Which variants went into the final essays is not stated.
RAPIDS was used to train the Ghostbuster classifiers much faster than scikit-learn.
Deep text embeddings of rules as extra features did not work well.
The whole team shared one validation scheme using 5-fold Group K-fold, following a public starter notebook's method.

technique_name: Use all training volumes including kidney_1_voi
technique_summary: All provided training data was used, explicitly including the kidney_1_voi volume.
Mistral 7B, both instruction-tuned and base, trained on different datasets, generated prompt predictions; Mistral was slightly better than Gemma.
For the earlier, replaced metric only, a differentiable approach optimized 237 small squares plus small text; not part of the final-metric solution.
Cosine annealing from 1e-4 to 0 with warmup; 20 epochs, or 30 for the 3D-rotation model.
AdamW optimizer with max LR 1e-3 and weight decay set to 4 times the LR.
MONAI random crop, flips on every axis and rotation were used; augmentation was essential because models were trained from scratch.
Heavy augmentation (rescale, 90-degree rotations, axis flips and swaps, coarse dropout, color inversion, mixup, cutmix) allowed 400 epochs without overfitting; LB stopped improving after 250.
Stage-one pre-training was BERT-style masked language modeling with 15% masking for about 100 epochs, using train, test and external SMILES together.
The solution was built starting from a blend of a prior-year Kaggle model and a public tutorial.
Knowledge distillation was listed among methods that did not improve CV.

N copies of each problem are sampled until a Python block, the code is executed and output appended, repeated M rounds with pruning of broken traces; N=48, M=4. It reduced variance versus earlier approaches.
Final submission was a weighted ensemble of ten backbone/strategy models, with per-model ensemble weights listed in a table.
The non-PII 'O' class was down-weighted (weight 0.05) instead of downsampling essays without PII.
The candidate keyword list of 116,937 nouns was built with NLTK, since keywords were specified to be things.

technique_name: Fold only RNA chains in complexes
technique_summary: For multi-chain targets, Boltz2 folds only the RNA chains to stay within memory.
Digit features are used in both feature sets, and combinations of digits are target-encoded (mean/std/skew) in feature set 1.

technique_name: ML-based denoising / channel weighting of input
technique_summary: ML methods to choose or weight spatial rows better than summing [8:24] were tried but none beat the simple sum.
A simple CutMix augmentation was applied with 15% probability.
Transformer models were tried but did not work.
Training used LLM-generated PII essay datasets from other Kagglers (the Mistral-generated set being most useful, plus a Mixtral8x7B set) and a self-generated 2k-sample set.
LightGBM on base+bin+digit+categorical+frequency features was among the frequently selected models.
CatBoost was the best model, which the author attributes to the roughly 117 categorical features.

technique_name: Tumor-patch fraction to detect normal cases
technique_summary: A patch-level logistic regression trained on binarized tumor annotations estimated tumor fraction to flag normal slides; it did not improve the public LB.
Trained a ReDrafter head on 100k target-model solutions; it drafted 3 tokens per step with 65% acceptance for about a 1.8x speedup.
Discretized numeric features with quantile bins, equal-width bins and simple rounding (e.g. Age/5, BP/10) to create diverse representations.
Edge extraction methods for transparent scenes were listed as ideas that did not work out.

technique_name: Per-day file storage and preallocated loading
technique_summary: Stored training data one HDF5 file per day and loaded it day by day into a preallocated array, avoiding the double memory of concatenation and enabling 300 features with online training.
The winning submission ensembles 13 varied models (LB 0.79410/0.79123), better than the best single model.
Used StratifiedGroupKFold with and without shuffling; CV gains above about 0.01 and gains from feature engineering tracked the LB better than small gains or parameter tuning.
PCA compresses the time-grid statistics to limit feature count and diversify from gap-based features.
Cross-entropy was chosen over BCE/focal after tuning, with unnormalized multi-hot labels so samples with more positives weigh more; author hypothesizes CE handles imbalance better.
Following Speedy MASt3R, TensorRT conversion was attempted to accelerate MASt3R, but the model could not be converted.
Ray Tune search over batch size, epochs, LR, hidden sizes and activations raised local CV but lowered public LB, so it was dropped.
Switching from DeBERTa-v3-base to the large variant gave little improvement.

The key factor was an incrementally built, diverse datamix of essays generated by proprietary, open-source and fine-tuned LLMs plus existing AI-text datasets; best models used 160k samples (40k human).
Dropout helped at ~1M samples but was unnecessary when ensembling at 40-80M samples, so it was removed for faster training.

technique_name: Mean prediction for poorly predicted targets
technique_summary: Targets with poor validation R2 would be replaced by the mean, but this turned out unnecessary since the only bad targets were already zeroed or ptend-handled.
An outcome reward model helped initially, but benefits diminished for long reasoning and TIR, especially on small sets such as 50 problems; not in the final submission.

technique_name: Direct signal regression without segmentation mask
technique_summary: Predicted ECG lead values numerically from CNN backbone features instead of first predicting a signal mask.

technique_name: Partial U-Net with loss on penultimate feature map
technique_summary: After analyzing the MONAI detection model, the author found the penultimate feature map was more accurate, so the U-Net decoder is truncated and the loss applied on a 48^3 output from 96^3 input patches.
Filtering stage-2 data to integer-only solutions was tried, but training on all solution types was slightly more robust, likely due to fewer samples after filtering.
Isotonic regression on OOF predictions (centered isotonic regression for most stacks, scikit-learn's for CatBoost) improved CV and LB by about 0.002.
All auxiliary tables except gas prices were merged into train (weather averaged per county) and many lag features were created, about 600 features in total without pruning.
GBDT and RGF models were retrained on all data with 20 seeds, n_estimators at 1.25x mean CV best iteration; better than averaging fold models.

First the stellar spectrum is fixed from temporal averaging, then it is freed and set optimally while initializing from stage-one parameters; per-point errors come from per-wavelength signal variation.
Several LightGBM models on 1,300+ engineered keystroke and essay features (CV ~0.589-0.598) are ensemble members.
The merged predictions of all combinations were blended by a weighted average whose weights were searched with Optuna under 5-fold CV.
LoRA on all linear layers (r=64, alpha=128) for the 9B model and QLoRA for the 70B/72B models.
Ran 2500 Optuna trials choosing subsets of about 150 OOF predictions to maximize OOF AUC; roughly a tenth were consistently picked.

technique_name: Mapping 16-bit weights to 8-bit codes via lookup tables
technique_summary: Per piece-type group, unique 16-bit weights were mapped to 8-bit codes (grouping rare values when slightly over 256) with reverse lookup arrays at load time, giving 8-bit storage without Elo loss.
A single multi-head self-attention layer fuses the concatenated left/right features, followed by an MLP.
Segmenting transparent objects before computing flow did not work out.
Grayscale pixel difference was tried as a pair weight for ordering but was superseded by the final SSIM + matching ensemble.
EVA02-small (eva02_small_patch14_336, a ViT variant) was one image model, chosen for a good metric/inference-time balance.
ALIKED keypoints and descriptors are cached per image, greatly reducing runtime.
The flip/inversion augmentation used by other top teams was missed; the author believes combining it with tree-search features could have scored better.
The curope RoPE2D extension was compiled with CUDA to accelerate MASt3R inference.
The selected submission ensembled two ConvNeXt-Tiny U-Nets differing only in augmentation and epochs; a single 3D-rotation model actually scored best on private LB (0.835) but was not selected.
The other selected final submission was a mean ensemble of 3 EfficientNet-B0 and 3 RegNetY models.

technique_name: Rule-based plus fitted transit time detection
technique_summary: The transit window is located on the wavelength-averaged signal, first approximately with rules and then precisely by fitting.

technique_name: Repeated CV with paired t-test for decisions
technique_summary: Changes were accepted only if a paired t-test over 10 seeded CV runs was significant and public LB agreed; late relaxation to p<0.2 and public LB reliance helped public but slightly hurt private.

technique_name: Mamba or self-attention instead of bi-LSTM
technique_summary: Replacing the bi-LSTM with Mamba or self-attention did not work.
XGBoost regressor and classifier were included as base models (CV 0.580 and 0.583).
A loss on max-pooled (kernel and stride 4) main outputs encouraged high probability near motors while tolerating small localization errors.
Both feature sets include a formula-derived feature from a linked source; the formula itself is not given in the text.
MSE, MSE/MAE combinations and weighted loss functions were worse than plain MAE.
The simulator's added foreground is estimated from the outer spatial rows [0:8] and [24:32] and subtracted from the central rows [8:24], replacing the ad-hoc 1.006-1.008 scaling trick.
Soundscapes were sampled with weight equal to the sum of per-label max probabilities, favouring more reliably labeled ones; a random 20 s window then received max-pooled soft labels.
From words of one target or shared by two targets, words are added (sorted by posting size) until the intersected patent set contains only targets; failures are discarded.
Mistral-7B-v0.1 sequence classifier fine-tuned on the datamix; it received the largest ensemble weight.
The faster sliding scheme freed time budget for test-time augmentation.
A random forest classifier on the Ghostbuster features, ensembled with the SVM, with little hyperparameter tuning.
Predictions were averaged across neighbouring chunks, one of the two most important inference steps.
10 s audio was converted to a 1x128x640 mel spectrogram (n_fft 1024, hop 500, 128 mels, 40-15000 Hz, power 2).

technique_name: Sparse match-result reward with partial point reward
technique_summary: Final reward was +/-1 per match result plus up to +/-2.5 per game for relic points; the partial point reward prevented do-nothing stagnation.
Models are trained on whole slices resized or cropped to 1536x1536 rather than on tiles.
Filtering mismatched image pairs with monocular depth estimates was listed among the things that did not work.

technique_name: Larger input resolution over larger model
technique_summary: Under limited compute, increasing input size helped more than scaling model size; best single models used 1024px per view with DINO-Large.
Larger holes are repaired by projecting each sheet to a height map along the axis with largest area and linearly interpolating gaps along x and y, blended by distance to the gap edge.
Adding Xeno-Canto samples under family-level insect labels to the main training worsened results; species-level labels in a dedicated model worked instead.
Chowder MIL on Phikon embeddings: TilesMLP hidden 192, ExtremeLayer top/bottom 10, final MLP hidden 96 with 30% dropout and sigmoid; hyperparameters chosen by hand.
CatBoost is one of three base models in the final ensemble, trained with extra-data weight 0.25.
An external CMU keystroke dataset was tried but never helped.
Solar features from a public notebook did not work.
Combined downsampling and upsampling CNNs with residual GRU layers.
Added minute embeddings directly to the final layer to capture event timing bias.
Used rolling sensor statistics and a rolling median of absolute angle differences.
Averaged overlapping daily chunks after trimming 30 minutes from their edges.
Constructed distance-decaying event targets and attenuated them each epoch to sharpen peaks.
Detected periodic device-removal intervals with rules and filtered inputs and predictions.
Trained minute-level second-stage tree and sequence models using first-stage predictions and sensor features.
Detected peaks in minute-averaged predictions and retained eight-minute neighborhoods for second-stage modeling.
Normalized second-stage predictions daily.
Scored candidate timestamps across evaluation tolerances and repeatedly selected the best point while discounting already covered probability mass.
Use one carefully crafted feature without fitting a machine learning model.
Exploit leaked peak time-to-failure information from test data.
Uses a transformer with 162M parameters, 18 layers, and four attention heads.
Applies test-time learning, with success on one illustrated test case and failure on the other.
Ensemble EfficientNets across image sizes and variants.
Tune on image size 128 with EfficientNet-B6 and transfer parameters to larger configurations.
Combine metadata with MLP-transformed EfficientNet outputs.
Use a class weight of 5.
Use fixed smoothing of 0.05 in conventional models.
Sample smoothing amounts randomly; the supplied code draws an absolute Gaussian value per batch. These models receive final ensemble weight 0.25.
Apply binary cross-entropy to randomly softened targets.
Include metadata-only and image-embedding-plus-metadata models.
Group correlated predictions, often by image size, and choose geometric means, medians, or the best single prediction using CV.
Grid-search blend weights on out-of-fold predictions after group averaging.
Adapted weighted boxes fusion to combine masks, matching predictions using bounding boxes.
Used detection models to improve ensemble confidence scores without generating masks.
Used Mask R-CNN with ConvNeXt and Swin backbones.
Included Cascade R-CNN with ConvNeXt backbones.
Used Mask2Former for segmentation and also as a detection-only contributor.
Included DINO, Diffusion Det, and ViT Det as detection models.
Mask addition and dilation favored rough public annotations but hurt private performance.
A post-competition correction replaced mask addition with voting and improved the private score to 0.575.
MaskDINO did not perform well.
YOLOX performed poorly; YOLO v7 and v8 were abandoned because their availability was unclear.
Trained B0–B7 at multiple image sizes, matching model capacity to suitable resolutions.
Used simple average ranks for both the 18-submission ensemble and the 12-model CV-selected ensemble.
Blended image predictions with Giba's baseline using weights of 0.4 and 0.6.
Combined binary cross-entropy with five times a focal-loss term.
Used focal loss with alpha 0.25 and gamma 2 alongside BCE; changing focal-loss class weights did not help.
Upsampling helped, although extreme 25-fold upsampling of 2020 malignant examples did not.
Included external 2018 data.
Applied GridMask augmentation, which performed better than coarse dropout.
Reported noisy-student training as helpful for some models.
Used early stopping with an 18-epoch training schedule for some models.
Training with 15 folds helped some models, and CV guided the strongest private-scoring ensemble.
Applied linked post-processing and then min-max post-processing to the public-score-focused ensemble; the author identified this pipeline as overfit.
Used subcenter ArcFace with dynamic margins.
Trained Swin Large models at multiple image sizes.
Trained ConvNeXt XLarge models using competition and external data.
Used ResNet200D with DOLG.
Used EfficientNet B6, B7, V2S, and V2M with DOLG.
Applied DOLG with several convolutional backbones.
Assigned FGVC9 labels to FGVC8 images using KNN matching and a threshold below 0.5.
Adjusted external pseudo-labels using hotel identity and mean aggregation.
Selected logits over nearest-neighbor inference because masked test images differed from training images.
Hotel50K data did not work.
Listed gradient checkpointing among approaches that did not work.
Each experimental round trains and validates five folds.
